## Research notes, round 2: LIN-3140 (re-check of the 2026-10-03 run and the FC note)

This was research only. Nothing was committed or pushed. All code was read at HEAD `4fd90d87` (2026-10-04). The spikes were throwaway and have been reverted, and `git status` is clean. This round builds on comment `06b35a6e` and tests the FC note `3868f87b`.

**Bottom line:** the FC note is right, and the hole is wider than it says. The bug isn't tied to a set of call sites. It is one branch of `establishAccount`: linking a *new, unowned* identity onto an already-live `session.accountId`. Any caller can reach that branch, including the "proof" callers' `mode:'new'` login callbacks, because they carry `accountId` across `regenerate()`. The 2026-10-03 classification (11 proof / 2 non-proof) is wrong. I now recommend fixing this inside `establishAccount`. A one-line spike passes the full unit suite (15732/0), closes every path, and makes the D1 save/restore redundant.

### Re-ground / staleness
- Since the ticket was created (`2026-09-29T09:30Z`), the cited paths only changed in LIN-3124/3125 connection work, LIN-1892 S3 and LIN-3243. Between the prior research HEAD `8e06243b` and `4fd90d87`, the only changes to `lib/` or `routes/` are `be9e0ec9` and `6bccd5c6` (LIN-3299, prompt-writer code), which have nothing to do with this.
- The stamp line is still at `lib/account-session.js:227`. `git log -S` shows it arrived only in `0c3dfd1e` (LIN-2233). `POST /workspace/new` still calls the seam at `routes/workspace.js:115`.

### Where the hole really is: establishAccount's four success branches
From `lib/account-session.js:114-229`:

| Branch | Condition | What it proves about the live account | Stamps today |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1: re-proof | `existingOwner` resolves to `session.accountId` (`:149-163`) | The person controls an identity P **already owned** before this request. This is a genuine re-proof of P. | yes |
| B2: front-door | `existingOwner`, no live `session.accountId` | Signs in **as** the owner. There is no prior account to be stale. | yes |
| B3: link-onto-live | `!existingOwner && session.accountId` (`:164-167`) | Only that the person controls the **new** identity, which is attached on the authority of the live session alone. **Says nothing about P.** | **yes, and this is the bug** |
| B4: mint (+ race adoption) | No owner, no live account (`:168-172`, adoption `:210-211`) | A brand-new account whose only identity was just proven. | yes |

Conflict returns (`:161`, `:190`) and `unknown-account` (`:198`) all exit before `:227`, so the 2026-10-03 finding still holds: a refused call never stamps. But a **successful** B3 call always stamps, and the FC note's point is exactly that "a conflict returns before the stamp" only covers the refused case.

### Spike 1: the hole is reachable from the "proof" callers (real route, real seam)
I drove the real `createAuthRoutes` `/auth/callback` handler over MangoDB, using the `tests/unit/auth-route.test.js` harness shape. Setup: stale P (`identityAuthenticatedAt: 0`, owns `linear:viewer-P`) and G (owns `linear:viewer-G`).

- **`mode:'add-source'` (`routes/auth.js:261`)**: P adds a brand-new `viewer-X`, which returns 200 and sets the stamp to **1 ms old**. A `mode:'new'` login as `viewer-G` then returns **409 `merge-confirm-page`**, with `pendingMerge` = {canonical P, merged G}.
- **`mode:'new'` front-door login (`routes/auth.js:404`)**: same result. The callback carries `accountId` and the stamp across `regenerate()` (`:361`, `:387`), so a new `viewer-X` takes B3, gets a 1 ms-old stamp, and then the conflict gives **409 `merge-confirm-page`**.

The 2026-10-03 table marked `routes/auth.js:404` as "Proof". It isn't when the arriving identity is new and P is live. The same carry-and-restore pattern exists at `lib/github-install-flow.js:873/894` (→ `:909`), `routes/jira-auth.js:820/849` (→ `:862`) and `routes/email-auth.js:570/582` (→ `:585`), and the in-code comments say the carry exists so that "a brand-new one arriving while this account is live" links onto it (`routes/auth.js:380-385`, `lib/github-install-flow.js:887-892`, `routes/jira-auth.js:842-847`).

### Spike 2: the fix inside the seam
The change at `lib/account-session.js:227` was `session.identityAuthenticatedAt = Date.now()` → `if (existingOwner || minted) session.identityAuthenticatedAt = Date.now()`. Under B3 this leaves the stamp exactly as it was (unchanged, or still absent).
- Spike 1, both modes: the stamp stays `0` and the conflict gives **`merge-reauth-required-page`** with no `pendingMerge`.
- `POST /workspace/new` (real route + real `respondToAccountConflict`):
  - With the stamp at `0` and with no stamp at all, the value is preserved exactly and the later conflict gives the re-auth page with no `pendingMerge`. That is 2/2.
  - On baseline both cases fail: the stamp is re-stamped (`1791103824676`), so the test is **fail-first**.
- **Full unit suite with the seam fix: 15732 pass / 0 fail** (`node --test tests/unit/*.test.js`, about 29 s). No existing test depends on B3 stamping.
- **D1 becomes redundant.** I applied the seam fix and also deleted the `completeLinkMode` restore (`routes/email-auth.js:266-269`). The email suites and `workspace-new-route` then pass 176/0, including all four D1/G4 tests in `email-link-mode-merge.test.js`. Control: deleting the D1 restore on baseline, without the seam fix, fails those same 4 tests. They are good mutation-killers and become the seam's regression tests.

### Spike 3: the remaining two-step bypass (out of scope, for the team)
With the seam fix applied: stale P adds new `viewer-X` (no stamp), then signs in **again** as `viewer-X`. X is now owned by P, so this takes B1 and re-stamps. The conflict then gives **409 `merge-confirm-page`** in both modes.

The root here is that **attaching an identity to a live account needs no freshness at all**. That is a policy gap separate from the stamp. The team has already accepted the email version of it: a link-mode attach (D1 restore) followed by a sign-in-mode confirm of that address is the "N2 positive control" that re-stamps P (`email-reproof-merge-witness.test.js:111`, `docs/architecture/auth.md:134-138`). The seam fix brings every provider and Local to the same standard D1 set for email, which is the scope of this ticket. Closing the two-step would mean gating B3 (identity attach) on A1 freshness. That changes the UX of add-source and linking for every stale session, so it is the team's call. See the question at the end.

### Layer audit (one brief per layer)
1. **Stamp seam, `lib/account-session.js:114-229`.** This is the one place the stamp is written for a successful sign-in. `existingOwner` (`:138`) and `minted` (`:141`, `:171`) are already locals in scope, so the fix needs no new state, type or field. Must keep: B1, B2 and B4 still stamp (pinned by `tests/unit/account-session.test.js:225,260`, `email-reproof*.test.js`, `email-auth-n2.test.js:204`). Also must keep: the race-equal fall-through (`:191-196`) reachable from B3 doesn't stamp, which is the conservative choice. The doc comments at `:37-46` and `:224-226`, and the `@returns`, should say "stamps only when the arriving identity proves the session's account (B1/B2/B4)".
2. **Gate, `lib/account-conflict.js:108-113`, `isFreshlyAuthenticated` (`lib/account-session.js:57-61`).** Unchanged. The confirm route re-checks freshness at confirm time (`routes/account-merge.js:96-97`). The fix only changes what the stamp means, and that meaning is the one the A1 docstring already claims: "the canonical side's own last proven identity link" (`:59-61`).
3. **Local caller, `routes/workspace.js:115`.** Always B3 when signed in (random `urlKey`, `:112-114`) and B4 when signed out. With the seam fix it needs **no change**, and the ticket's acceptance is met without editing this file. Its regression test still belongs in `tests/unit/workspace-new-route.test.js`.
4. **Email link mode, `routes/email-auth.js:255-269` (D1).** Always B3 or B1. Its restore becomes a no-op on success under the seam fix. B1 (address already on P) previously got its stamp restored, i.e. *not* refreshed. Under the seam fix B1 would refresh. That is a **tiny behaviour change**: a link-mode confirm of an address already on P would now count as a re-proof. Recommendation: **keep the D1 restore** as defence in depth (it has zero cost, and link mode is "not a sign-in" by its own ruling), and update its comment so it no longer says the seam stamps on every success. Delete it only if the team prefers one mechanism. Either way the D1 tests stay green, as shown above.
5. **Email sign-in, `routes/email-auth.js:562-585`.** The N2 gate (`:562-564`) admits a live account only when the address is already on it, so the result is always B1, B2 or B4 and never B3. Genuine proof, unchanged.
6. **Linear, `routes/auth.js:261` (add-source) and `:404` (`mode:'new'` with carry `:361-387`).** Both reach B3 (Spike 1). The conflict arms use `respondToAccountConflict` (`:278`, `:391`). After the fix: a new identity links with no stamp, and a returning identity on P (B1) still stamps.
7. **GitHub, `lib/github-install-flow.js:747` (add-source, non-merge conflict page `:748-750`), `:819` (existing `github:<userId>` container, live session), `:909` (fresh/new container, carry `:873-894`).** All can reach B3 on success, and a stamp they set feeds the *other* arms' merge gates. Covered by the seam fix.
8. **Jira, `routes/jira-auth.js:287` (Basic link, validates `/myself`), `:593` (OAuth add-source), `:771` (existing container), `:862` (new login, carry `:820-849`).** Same as GitHub. Validating `/myself` proves the Jira identity, not P.
9. **PAT, `lib/pat-session.js:96`.** Server-config PAT auto-login. It resets `session.workspaces` (`:90`) but not `accountId`, so it reaches B3 only if a live account doesn't already own that viewer. The deployment's PAT holder is the operator, so this is low risk, and the seam fix covers it anyway.
10. **Deliberate non-stampers.** `routes/held-connection.js:314-316` (F8) and `lib/connection-credential.js:1160` don't call the seam, and the tests pin "no freshness stamp" (`lin-3125-picker-route.test.js:354`, `lin-3125-held-connection-witness.test.js:270`). Unaffected.
11. **Test-only router, `routes/test.js`.** Mounted only under `NODE_ENV==='test'` (`server.js:956-961`). Its seeding callers that link a second identity onto a live session will stop stamping. The full suite, including every Playwright-seed consumer reachable from the unit suite, is green. **E2E (Playwright) was not run.** The plan should run `npm test` (unit + e2e) on the implementation PR, because an e2e merge spec that seeds P via a B3 path and expects a merge offer would now see the re-auth page. I read the only e2e merge fixture, `/test/set-merge-conflict-session` (`routes/test.js:354-410`). Its canonical side C is minted (B4) on the request's session, so it still stamps. A spec that chains seed routes on one session before a merge is the residual risk.
12. **Docs, `docs/architecture/auth.md`.** It doesn't currently state the A1 stamp rule (only `:140` mentions the carry). Add one sentence on what stamps freshness.

### Class sweep (bounded)
**Class A: production `establishAccount` callers.** Bounded by `grep -rn "establishAccount(" lib routes server.js` excluding `routes/test.js`. There are 13 callers (same set as round 1), now classified by **reachable branch**, not by call site:

| Site | Reaches B3 (non-proof success)? |
|---|---|
| `routes/workspace.js:115` | **yes, always when signed in** |
| `routes/email-auth.js:265` (link) | **yes** (D1-restored today) |
| `routes/auth.js:261` | **yes (spiked)** |
| `routes/auth.js:404` | **yes (spiked)** |
| `lib/github-install-flow.js:747`, `:819`, `:909` | yes (same carry/link shape) |
| `routes/jira-auth.js:287`, `:593`, `:771`, `:862` | yes (same shape) |
| `lib/pat-session.js:96` | yes in principle, operator-only |
| `routes/email-auth.js:585` (sign-in) | **no**: the N2 gate rules out B3 |

So 12 of 13 can make a non-proof success. Fixing per call site would need 12 save/restore copies; fixing in the seam needs one line.

**Class B: success branches of `establishAccount` that stamp.** Bounded by reading `:114-229`: B1, B2, B3, B4, and the race fall-through (from B1 or B3). That is the complete set, since every success path converges on `:219-228`.

**Class C: consumers of the stamp.** Bounded by `grep -rn identityAuthenticatedAt lib routes server.js`: the writer `lib/account-session.js:227`; readers `isFreshlyAuthenticated` (`lib/account-session.js:57-61`) → `lib/account-conflict.js:108` and `routes/account-merge.js:96`; carriers `routes/auth.js:361/387`, `lib/github-install-flow.js:873/894`, `routes/jira-auth.js:820/849`, `routes/email-auth.js:570/582`; clearers `clearUnresolvableAccountSession` (`lib/account-session.js:74-79`); the restorer `routes/email-auth.js:264-269`. None of them needs a change for the seam fix. Freshness only matters for a merge offer or confirm.

**Closure.** If I missed something, it would be a success path that writes `session.accountId` *without* the seam, or a second writer of the stamp. `grep -rn "identityAuthenticatedAt *=" lib routes server.js` returns only the seam and the carry/restore sites listed above. `grep -rn "session.accountId *=" lib routes` returns the seam (`:128`, `:223`), the four regenerate carries, and the merge-confirm A2 write (`routes/account-merge.js:214`, already behind the freshness gate).

### Options
| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Per-site save/restore at `routes/workspace.js` only (2026-10-03 rec.)** | Smallest diff, follows the ticket text | Leaves at least 11 other B3-reachable callers open (Spike 1 proves 2 of them); it would be a third copy of the workaround |
| B. Save/restore at all 12 B3-reachable sites | No seam edit | 12 copies of the same workaround; any new caller is unsafe by default; it fights the seam's "one place" design |
| **C. Branch-aware stamp in `establishAccount` (recommended)** | One line at the cause; covers every current and future caller; no new state; full suite 15732/0; D1 tests still green | Overrides the ticket's "leave `lib/account-session.js` unchanged". That guidance assumed provider paths need the stamp on every success, and the suite shows they don't |
| D. C plus gate B3 (identity attach) on freshness | Also closes the two-step (Spike 3) | Changes add-source/link UX for every stale session; a policy decision; out of this ticket's scope |

### Surface Assessment
`Surface Assessment: [refactor required: make the freshness stamp in establishAccount branch-aware (stamp only on B1/B2/B4, never on B3 link-onto-live) — reason: removes this task's confirmed cause at lib/account-session.js:227, which Spike 1 shows is reachable from at least two more callers than /workspace/new]`

- **Cause-or-consumer test:** the cause is the unconditional write at `lib/account-session.js:227`, which runs on B3 (`:164-167`). The change removes it there. Spike 2 shows the `/workspace/new` repro and both Linear repros flip to the re-auth page.
- **Who-pays test:**
  - Beneficiaries: all 12 B3-reachable callers become correct. `routes/workspace.js` needs no edit. `routes/email-auth.js` D1 becomes defence in depth.
  - Unchanged: B1, B2 and B4 callers (every genuine sign-in and re-proof), the gate, the confirm route, and the held-connection path.
  - Bystander tax: a legitimate **stale** user who links a new identity and then hits a conflict within 10 minutes now gets the re-auth page instead of a merge offer. That is the intended A1 behaviour, and the same thing D1 already imposes for email. A local-only P with no other identity has no re-proof route after 10 minutes, which matches `linkModeReproof`'s existing "local-only P gets no url" (`routes/email-auth.js:225`).
- **Size:** about 1 line of code plus comments, docs and tests, so it fits one implementation session. Per this verdict it's a blocking prep step, but it is small enough that the plan can run it as the first step of the same PR.

### Question for the team (non-blocking for this ticket)
Should **attaching** a new identity to a live account (B3) itself require A1 freshness? Without that, a left-open session can attach the sitting party's identity X and then re-sign in as X to get a fresh P (Spike 3). Today this is accepted for email as the N2 positive control. **My recommendation:** file it as its own follow-up ticket (policy/UX). Land the seam fix here, since it closes the one-step hole on every path and is strictly tighter than today.

## Implementation landed — PR #1746

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/1746
**Branch:** `feat/lin-3140-b3-branch-aware-stamp` (commit `5912df9c`)
**CI:** all green — `CI success`, Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, secret scan (run 37193693078)

### What changed
The confirmed cause was at the seam, as the 2026-10-04 research found: `establishAccount` unconditionally stamped `session.identityAuthenticatedAt` on every success, including B3 (link a new, unowned identity onto an already-live `session.accountId`). Made the stamp branch-aware:

```js
if (existingOwner || minted) session.identityAuthenticatedAt = Date.now();
```

Stamps on B1/B2/B4; never on B3, preserving the prior value exactly (including absent). `routes/workspace.js` needed no change; the `completeLinkMode` D1 restore stays as defence in depth with an updated comment; one paragraph added to `docs/architecture/auth.md`.

### Evidence
- **Fail-first on baseline:** 6 new tests failed. e.g. `POST /workspace/new` left the stamp at `1791107618241` instead of `0`; absent became `1791107618247` instead of `undefined`.
- **Fixed:** those 6 pass; B1/B2/B4 still stamp.
- Full unit suite: **15745 pass / 0 fail**. Hermetic suite: **PASS — zero non-loopback sockets**.
- E2E account-merge spec unaffected (its canonical side C is minted → B4 → still stamps).

### Out of scope
The two-step bypass (stale P attaches identity X, then re-signs in as X) remains a separate policy/UX question about gating B3 attach on A1 freshness, as recommended.

## Review — LIN-3140

Reviewed PR #1746 (https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/1746) at head `5912df9c`, base `4fd90d87` (current `origin/main`, MERGEABLE).

CI: green on head `5912df9c`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success, all SUCCESS.

### Scope vs plan
The diff matches the 2026-10-04 research recommendation (option C) and the implementation note. Six files changed: `lib/account-session.js` (branch-aware stamp plus comments), `routes/email-auth.js` (comment only, D1 restore kept), `docs/architecture/auth.md` (+1 paragraph) and three test files. `routes/workspace.js` is untouched, as planned. Nothing goes beyond the plan.

### Correctness (read at head)
`if (existingOwner || minted) session.identityAuthenticatedAt = Date.now();` I traced it through every success path of `establishAccount`:
- B1/B2 (`existingOwner` set; a live mismatch returns a conflict before the stamp) → stamps.
- B3 (`!existingOwner && session.accountId`) → `minted` is false → the stamp is untouched, including when absent.
- B4 mint, and mint-race adoption (`minted` stays true) → stamps.
- Race fall-through with an equal owner, which only runs when `!minted`: from B1 it stamps, from B3 it doesn't. That is the conservative direction, and it holds by construction on both locals.

Writer sweep (`grep "identityAuthenticatedAt *=" lib routes server.js`): only the seam, the four pre-`establishAccount` regenerate carries (which restore the *prior* value) and the D1 restore. No other writer can re-stamp after B3. This matches research's Class C.

### Regression check
`git log origin/main -- lib/account-session.js routes/email-auth.js docs/architecture/auth.md`: the stamp line came only from `0c3dfd1e` (LIN-2233). The LIN-2285 canonicalisation and race-branch logic are unchanged. There are no reverts in range, and the LIN-1892 S3 D1 restore is kept. No earlier fix is re-introduced or undone.

### Tests and mutation check (LIN-2274)
The four touched or relevant suites (`account-session`, `auth-route`, `workspace-new-route`, `email-link-mode-merge`) pass **74/0** at head, re-run by me. Mutations, each reverted afterwards:
- **M1:** stamp unconditionally (the baseline behaviour) → **6 fail**: both seam B3 tests, both `/workspace/new` tests (stale and absent) and both Linear route tests (`add-source` and `mode:'new'`). Fail-first confirmed.
- **M2:** `if (existingOwner)` only → "B4 mint still stamps" plus 7 existing merge and null-workspace tests fail.
- **M3:** `if (minted)` only → "B1 re-proof" and "B2 front-door" tests fail.

The load-bearing tests assert the right thing. The test levels fit: the seam has unit tests, and the real route handlers (`/workspace/new`, Linear `/auth/callback`) are chained into the real `respondToAccountConflict`. The E2E merge spec ran green in CI, which settles research's residual Playwright risk.

**Finding (non-blocking, outside the bounded class):** with the seam fix in place, I deleted the D1 restore at `routes/email-auth.js:269-270`. All `tests/unit/email-*.test.js` still pass, **167/0**. Under the seam fix the restore's only live effect is the B1 case: link mode for an address already on P. That case is reachable, because `POST` link mode has no "already on P" guard, unlike `reproof`. The new comment says D1 "deliberately never moves P's freshness even in the B1 case", but no test pins that. There is no A1 hole here. A B1 link proves control of an address P already owns, the same proof S3-4 re-proof accepts and re-stamps on. So this is a coverage gap on a defence-in-depth branch, not this ticket's defect.

### Class check
The class is a successful non-proof `establishAccount` branch refreshing A1 freshness. Every instance (the 12 B3-reachable production callers) is closed by the one seam change. Linear add-source and `mode:'new'` are proven at route level, and the rest are covered structurally by the seam tests plus the writer sweep. The two-step bypass (attach X, then sign in again as X → B1) is a different policy question, not this class. It is already covered by the open ruling `lin3140-b3-attach-freshness` (recommended: file a follow-up), so I am not raising it again here.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside:** B3 race fall-through (`linkIdentity` race, equal owner, coming from B3) leaves the stamp untouched. CI does not reach this path. **Discharged** by inspection: `existingOwner` is null and `minted` is false on that path, so the predicate is false by construction.
- **Inside:** GitHub (`lib/github-install-flow.js:747/819/909`), Jira (`routes/jira-auth.js:287/593/771/862`) and PAT (`lib/pat-session.js:96`) B3 callers do not re-stamp. They have no route-level test. **Discharged** by the seam unit tests plus the writer sweep above: none of these callers writes the stamp after `establishAccount`.
- **Outside, for close-out to file after checking it doesn't exist:** "Pin or remove the email link-mode D1 freshness restore (`routes/email-auth.js` `completeLinkMode`)." Since LIN-3140 made `establishAccount` stamp only on B1/B2/B4, the restore affects only link-mode confirms of an address already on the live account (B1). Deleting it keeps every email test green. Either add a test asserting that a link-mode confirm of an address already on P leaves `identityAuthenticatedAt` unchanged (stale and absent cases), or remove the restore and its comment if the team accepts that a B1 link counts as a re-proof.
- **Outside, already tracked:** the two-step B3-attach bypass → ruling `lin3140-b3-attach-freshness` (open). Close-out acts on its answer and needs no new filing from this review.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

The cause is fixed at the seam with the minimum change. Fail-first tests were verified by mutation at seam and route level, CI is green including E2E, and the remaining ledger items are already discharged or are outside follow-ups that close-out can route.

issue.title: Give the next-stage choice a place of its own
issue.description:
Harbour chooses which stage a ticket needs next inside the meta call, the call that used to write the whole prompt. Since LIN-3299, code assembles the prompt, so choosing the stage is that call's main remaining job. But the choice is still tangled up with the old prompt-writing half. That makes it hard to see what the choice is based on, what it hands to the next stage, or how good it is.

The first live run of the new prompts (LIN-3140, 4 Oct; summary on LIN-3289) went well inside each stage. What slipped were judgements about the next step.

The aim is to make the next-stage choice its own clear, measured piece: something that can be improved and trusted on its own, leaving the rest of the prompt path simpler. A wrong route matters; a suboptimal one is fine.

Every recommendation passes through this choice, so measure before changing how it behaves.

Related: LIN-3300, LIN-3301.

parent.title: Split prompt assembly from prompt writing, and let agents fix at the cause

comments.body:
## Research notes: LIN-3304, the next-stage choice (4 Oct, HEAD `75b5c924`)

**Staleness check.** Nothing under `lib/`, `routes/`, `scripts/` or `docs/` has changed on `origin/main` since the ticket was created (10:43). The ticket's claims still hold at HEAD.

### The questions this research answered
1. What does the choice read, and how much of that is implicit?
2. What does it hand on, and to whom?
3. Where is it still tangled with prompt-writing?
4. Can it be measured today, and would the measurement track a *wrong* route?
5. What was tried before?

---

### Per-layer audit

**L1. Router prompt (`lib/prompts/meta-prompt-template.js`)**
- Routing-only mode is not a prompt of its own. It is the full template with the writing blocks blanked: `const W = (text) => routingOnly ? '' : text;` (meta:81). It only removes text; nothing is added.
- **Routing sections, kept in both modes:**
  - facts (96-104)
  - role (106)
  - Task Context (110)
  - Sequential Workflow Decision with Steps 0-4 (128-240)
  - Action Types Reference (308-312) and Completion Signals (313-321)
  - instructions 1-2 (333-335)
  - reply skeleton (338-348) and action/DeferTo rules (352-354)
- **Writing sections, W-gated:** 113-127, 132, 241-307 (about 60 KB of quality rules), 322-332, 336, 349-351, 355.
- **Size**, with empty issue context:

  | Case | Routing-only | Full |
  |---|---|---|
  | Leaf | 41.6 KB | 103 KB |
  | Node | 49 KB | 111 KB |

  The issue context is unbounded on top of that: the full description and every comment (openrouter.js:623-636, 759-763).
- **Writing text left inside the routing half:**
  - meta:183 says "the generated prompt should skip full analysis", about a prompt this call no longer writes.
  - meta:143-144 say what review and close-out *write*.
  - meta:239 restates the defer no-body rule.
- **Trail-shaping rules** sit in the W half: plan-review due, session fit, the verdict format, "name the next action" (meta:132, 293, 298-304). The router reads these back later. Routing-only still works because code now owns them: `lib/prompt-contract.js` carries `plan-review due` and `Plan Review Verdict`, and `prompt-template-defs.js` carries session fit and next stage. I checked these by grep.

**L2. Router inputs (`buildMetaPrompt`, openrouter.js:784-841; `formatIssueContext`, 646-775)**
- Everything reaches the model as one prose user message at temperature 0 (openrouter.js:2211-2216). There is no structured input.
- **Explicit, computed by code:**
  - child counts, `isTerminal`, `hasOpenChildren`, and frontier facts with `nextChild` (`assembleNodeFacts`, recommendation-facts.js:89-101)
  - `sessionFit`, pulled from the description by regex (recommendation-facts.js:47-52)
  - the focused child, from `selectFocusSubtask` (tree.js:249-297)
  - Code also picks which Step 0 variant the model sees (meta:135-150).

issue.title: Give the next-stage choice a place of its own
issue.description:
Harbour chooses which stage a ticket needs next inside the meta call, the call that used to write the whole prompt. Since LIN-3299, code assembles the prompt, so choosing the stage is that call's main remaining job. But the choice is still tangled up with the old prompt-writing half. That makes it hard to see what the choice is based on, what it hands to the next stage, or how good it is.

The first live run of the new prompts (LIN-3140, 4 Oct; summary on LIN-3289) went well inside each stage. What slipped were judgements about the next step.

The aim is to make the next-stage choice its own clear, measured piece: something that can be improved and trusted on its own, leaving the rest of the prompt path simpler. A wrong route matters; a suboptimal one is fine.

Every recommendation passes through this choice, so measure before changing how it behaves.

Related: LIN-3300, LIN-3301.

issue.title: Give the next-stage choice a place of its own
issue.description:
Harbour chooses which stage a ticket needs next inside the meta call, the call that used to write the whole prompt. Since LIN-3299, code assembles the prompt, so choosing the stage is that call's main remaining job. But the choice is still tangled up with the old prompt-writing half. That makes it hard to see what the choice is based on, what it hands to the next stage, or how good it is.

The first live run of the new prompts (LIN-3140, 4 Oct; summary on LIN-3289) went well inside each stage. What slipped were judgements about the next step.

The aim is to make the next-stage choice its own clear, measured piece: something that can be improved and trusted on its own, leaving the rest of the prompt path simpler. A wrong route matters; a suboptimal one is fine.

Every recommendation passes through this choice, so measure before changing how it behaves.

Related: LIN-3300, LIN-3301.

  | Leaf | 41.6 KB | 103 KB |
  | Node | 49 KB | 111 KB |

  - the focused child, from `selectFocusSubtask` (tree.js:249-297)
  - Code also picks which Step 0 variant the model sees (meta:135-150).

  - whether a bug was already investigated (184-188)

  - ledgers
  - `stateTransitions`, which are fetched (linear/index.js:947-954) but go unused

**L3. Router output contract and parse (openrouter.js:1733-1834)**
- The reply is markdown, not JSON: `## Reasoning`, then Assessment, optional Signal Status, `→ **<action>**`, optional `**DeferTo:**`, and `**Next:**`.
- The action comes from a regex on the reasoning text (`parseRecommendedAction`, 1733). The defer target comes from `parseDeferTo` (1752).

  |---|---|---|

  - Cause: routing-only is a subtractive mask over the writing template (meta:81). One parser serves two modes with different rules for an unknown action (openrouter.js:1774-1834 vs 2162). Writing text sits in the routing half (meta:183).
  - Consumer: step 1's routing-only eval arm and the trace annotation both call `routeStage`/`parseRouteDecision`.
- **Who-pays test**

  | Consumer | Role | Effect |
  |---|---|---|
  | `getRecommendation` / `getRecommendationStream` | beneficiary | simpler |
  | The four routed surfaces and the descent | unchanged | they consume the same `parsed` shape |
  | Writer-off full path | bystander | new obligation: byte-identical output, already pinned by `prompt-size-budget` and `meta-prompt.baseline.txt`; no runtime cost |
  | Eval harnesses | beneficiary | |

  No unjustified tax.
- This is not a second representation: the decision object *is* today's `parsed` object (openrouter.js:1814-1819) with the fields the parser already reads, given one owner.

**Scope for this ticket (John, 4 Oct):** a plain refactor. Move the next-stage choice into its own place behind one clear function, with behaviour unchanged, and point the existing routing evals at it.

The research is good. Pin today's routing prompts byte for byte before moving anything, so "unchanged" is proven, not argued.

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/1747  
**Commit:** `a200f843`  
**CI:** green — Unit tests, all 4 E2E shards, Secret scan, and CI success all pass (run 37197914157).

A plain refactor, behaviour unchanged. Full and routing-only renders match the pre-change output byte for byte on leaf, node-with-frontier-facts, and terminal-node fixtures (sha256 in the PR). New `tests/unit/stage-router.test.js` asserts `buildRouterPrompt(args) === buildMetaPromptTemplate({...args, routingOnly:true})` and that the full template still carries every fragment.

### Behaviour deliberately unchanged (pinned, fix owed later)
The two confirmed defects are pinned as **present**, not fixed: the live `**Reasoning**` header still parses in routing mode, and an out-of-list `retro` is still accepted.

### Acceptance witness
Ran the new tests against mutated code and captured failures: dropping a fragment broke byte-identity; neutering the `**Next:**` parse broke `routeStage`; removing the bold-`Reasoning` fallback broke the behaviour pin. All restored.

### Evals pointed at the seam
`scripts/eval-plan-review.mjs` imports the parser from `lib/stage-router.js`; the entry-point harnesses (`jev-routing-eval.mjs` arm 3, `brief-writer-compare.mjs`) read the decision through `getRecommendation`, which now calls the seam. `eval-research-routing.mjs` is deliberately decoupled (plain-text) and left as-is.

`npm run test:unit` 15755 pass / 0 fail; `test:hermetic` and `test:hermetic:proxy` PASS (zero non-loopback sockets); `secret-scan` PASS.

Merging is left to review + close-out.

## Review — LIN-3304

I reviewed head `a200f843` (PR #1747, branch `feat/lin-3304-stage-router-seam`, based on `75b5c924`).

CI: green on `a200f843`. Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and CI success all pass.

### Scope against the plan
The scope matches John's ruling: a plain refactor plus repointed evals. The diff touches 8 files, and none of them fix the deferred defects or change the measurement work. The staleness check came back clean: nothing under `lib/`, `scripts/`, `docs/` or `tests/` changed on `main` after the ticket was created.

### Regression check
`git log -30` on `openrouter.js`, `meta-prompt-template.js` and the three eval scripts shows recent LIN-3299, LIN-3293 and LIN-3294 commits. Nothing those commits fixed comes back, and none of them were reverts.

### Findings

**1. `buildRouterPrompt` drops the provider capability pass, so routing-only is not byte-identical for non-Linear providers (inside: a claim this ticket's own change depends on, "behaviour unchanged / byte-identical").**
`buildMetaPromptTemplate` ends with `applyPromptCapabilities(metaPrompt, …)`. That pass renames the tracker to the provider's `displayName`, strips ` in {tracker}`, and shapes fixed-state wording. `buildRouterPrompt` (`lib/stage-router.js:272-275`) only concatenates the fragments. `buildMetaPrompt` now sends `buildRouterPrompt` whenever the brief writer is on (`openrouter.js:845-850`).

I compared base `75b5c924` with the PR across 11 argument sets:
- The full prompt and the meta template's own `routingOnly` output are byte-identical in every case.
- `buildRouterPrompt` differs from base for `providerUi.displayName` `GitHub Issues` and `Local`. The role line now says "…next action on a **Linear** task." where base said "…on a **GitHub Issues** task."
- Who is affected: GitHub, GitHub Projects and Local workspaces with the brief writer on.
- Why tests miss it: every fixture in `tests/unit/stage-router.test.js` uses the default provider.

Fix:
- Make `buildRouterPrompt` take `featureFlags`/`providerUi` and apply `applyPromptCapabilities(…, { ...resolvePromptUi(featureFlags, providerUi), write: true, subtasks: true })`, the same pass as the meta template. Alternatively, run that pass once in a shared helper.
- Add the byte-identity case `{ providerUi: { displayName: 'GitHub Issues' } }` (and `linearMcp: false`) to the seam test.

**2. "Writer-off" is inverted throughout the new prose (inside: this ticket's own docs and comments).**
Routing-only is the **writer-on** path: `const writer = options.briefWriter ? … : null; buildMetaPrompt(…, !!writer)` (`openrouter.js:2166-2169`). The new text says the opposite in 8 places:
- the `stage-router.js` header (twice)
- the `routerFragments` doc
- the `buildRouterPrompt` doc
- the `parseRouteDecision` doc
- `docs/architecture/source-map.md`
- the `brief-writer-compare.mjs` header
- the `jev-routing-eval.mjs` header
- the stage-router test header

The PR body says "writer-on" correctly. The ticket's distilled brief has already picked up "writer-off router prompt". Fix: replace "writer-off" with "writer-on" (routing-only) in each of these.

**3. The `jev-routing-eval.mjs` arm 3 header overstates the claim (inside: "point the existing routing evals at it").**
Arm 3 calls `getRecommendation(…, { featureFlags: {} })` with no `briefWriter` (`jev-routing-eval.mjs:366`). So it runs the full prompt and the full-mode `parseRecommendationResponse`. It never goes through `buildRouterPrompt` or `routeStage`; it only shares the moved fragments and `parseRecommendedAction`.

Moving arm 3 onto the routing-only path would be the measurement change the ruling deferred, so leaving its behaviour alone is right. Fix: change the header so it says the arm still measures the full path through the shared fragments, rather than "the writer-off parse now comes from lib/stage-router.js". `eval-research-routing.mjs` staying decoupled is fine for a plain refactor.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is "a routing-only prompt built outside `buildMetaPromptTemplate` skips that function's post-processing". `buildRouterPrompt` is its only member: no other caller builds a meta prompt outside the template (I grepped `buildRouterPrompt|buildMetaPromptTemplate|routerFragments`). The class sits inside this ticket, as finding 1.

### Test quality and mutation check (each change reverted, worktree left clean)
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Change a shared fragment sentence in `stage-router.js` | **Red**: the full-prompt baseline test fails |
| Buffered writer path parses with full-mode `parseRecommendationResponse` instead of `routeStage` | **Red**: `brief-writer-route` and `brief-writer-wiring` fail; the wiring file then hangs |
| Stream writer path, same swap | **Red**: 2 failures, including the stream switch-on test |
| `buildMetaPrompt` sends the full template when routing only | **Red**: "the routing call asks for no body and carries no stage rules" |
| (implementer's three, per the PR) | reported red |

Verdicts on the tests:
- The load-bearing tests are real; the call sites into the seam are guarded.
- One gap: the `buildRouterPrompt === buildMetaPromptTemplate({routingOnly:true})` test compares new code with new code. It proves the two composers agree, not that routing-only equals the pre-change output. The full-prompt baseline covers the fragment text, and nothing covers the post-processing, which is exactly how finding 1 slipped through.
- I re-ran `tests/unit/stage-router.test.js` locally: 10 of 10 pass.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Routing-only prompt for non-Linear providers matches pre-change bytes. Inside** (finding 1; this ticket's byte-identity claim). Not discharged: it needs a code change plus a test, which is beyond close-out's trivial-edit bound.
- **Prose accuracy: "writer-off" wording and the arm 3 header. Inside** (findings 2–3; this ticket's own docs and comments). Discharge: the exact edits named above, done in implementation along with finding 1.
- **The live writer-on recommend path in a real workspace still routes the same. Inside** (behaviour unchanged). No test can prove model behaviour on live traffic, so this takes the post-merge observation lane:
  - Monitor: `prompt-traces` rows for writer-on hops. Their stored `metaPrompt` should equal `buildMetaPromptTemplate({...args, routingOnly:true})` for the same input.
  - The proxy log line `Proxy /recommend error: Invalid response: missing ## Reasoning or recommended action` fires if the parse regresses.
  - Rollback: revert `a200f843`. No migration, no persisted new shape, no coordinated release.

### Verdict
**Request Changes.** The refactor is sound and well guarded on the Linear path, but `buildRouterPrompt` skips the provider capability pass. That breaks the ticket's "behaviour unchanged / byte-identical" claim for GitHub and Local workspaces with the writer on. Fixing it needs a code change and a test, so this goes back to `implementation`. Do findings 2 and 3 (the wording) in the same pass. Then review re-runs.

**Addendum to the review: two items from this ticket's scope it didn't ask for.**

1. **Real byte snapshots of both routing prompts** (writer on and writer off), checked in as expected text. Include a provider other than Linear and the Step 0 variants, so that a one-character change fails. The current seam test compares new code with new code, so it can't catch a text change.
2. **Keep the size freeze binding.** Lower the meta template's ceiling to its new size, and give `stage-router.js` a ceiling of its own.

Make the fixes on PR #1747's existing branch, not in a new PR.

issue.title: Give the next-stage choice a place of its own
issue.description:
Harbour chooses which stage a ticket needs next inside the meta call, the call that used to write the whole prompt. Since LIN-3299, code assembles the prompt, so choosing the stage is that call's main remaining job. But the choice is still tangled up with the old prompt-writing half. That makes it hard to see what the choice is based on, what it hands to the next stage, or how good it is.

The first live run of the new prompts (LIN-3140, 4 Oct; summary on LIN-3289) went well inside each stage. What slipped were judgements about the next step.

The aim is to make the next-stage choice its own clear, measured piece: something that can be improved and trusted on its own, leaving the rest of the prompt path simpler. A wrong route matters; a suboptimal one is fine.

Every recommendation passes through this choice, so measure before changing how it behaves.

Related: LIN-3300, LIN-3301.

parent.title: Split prompt assembly from prompt writing, and let agents fix at the cause

comments.body:
## Research notes: LIN-3304, the next-stage choice (4 Oct, HEAD `75b5c924`)

**Staleness check.** Nothing under `lib/`, `routes/`, `scripts/` or `docs/` has changed on `origin/main` since the ticket was created (10:43). The ticket's claims still hold at HEAD.

### The questions this research answered
1. What does the choice read, and how much of that is implicit?
2. What does it hand on, and to whom?
3. Where is it still tangled with prompt-writing?
4. Can it be measured today, and would the measurement track a *wrong* route?
5. What was tried before?

---

### Per-layer audit

**L1. Router prompt (`lib/prompts/meta-prompt-template.js`)**
- Routing-only mode is not a prompt of its own. It is the full template with the writing blocks blanked: `const W = (text) => routingOnly ? '' : text;` (meta:81). It only removes text; nothing is added.
- **Routing sections, kept in both modes:**
  - facts (96-104)
  - role (106)
  - Task Context (110)
  - Sequential Workflow Decision with Steps 0-4 (128-240)
  - Action Types Reference (308-312) and Completion Signals (313-321)
  - instructions 1-2 (333-335)
  - reply skeleton (338-348) and action/DeferTo rules (352-354)
- **Writing sections, W-gated:** 113-127, 132, 241-307 (about 60 KB of quality rules), 322-332, 336, 349-351, 355.
- **Size**, with empty issue context:

  | Case | Routing-only | Full |
  |---|---|---|
  | Leaf | 41.6 KB | 103 KB |
  | Node | 49 KB | 111 KB |

  The issue context is unbounded on top of that: the full description and every comment (openrouter.js:623-636, 759-763).
- **Writing text left inside the routing half:**
  - meta:183 says "the generated prompt should skip full analysis", about a prompt this call no longer writes.
  - meta:143-144 say what review and close-out *write*.
  - meta:239 restates the defer no-body rule.
- **Trail-shaping rules** sit in the W half: plan-review due, session fit, the verdict format, "name the next action" (meta:132, 293, 298-304). The router reads these back later. Routing-only still works because code now owns them: `lib/prompt-contract.js` carries `plan-review due` and `Plan Review Verdict`, and `prompt-template-defs.js` carries session fit and next stage. I checked these by grep.

**L2. Router inputs (`buildMetaPrompt`, openrouter.js:784-841; `formatIssueContext`, 646-775)**
- Everything reaches the model as one prose user message at temperature 0 (openrouter.js:2211-2216). There is no structured input.
- **Explicit, computed by code:**
  - child counts, `isTerminal`, `hasOpenChildren`, and frontier facts with `nextChild` (`assembleNodeFacts`, recommendation-facts.js:89-101)
  - `sessionFit`, pulled from the description by regex (recommendation-facts.js:47-52)
  - the focused child, from `selectFocusSubtask` (tree.js:249-297)
  - Code also picks which Step 0 variant the model sees (meta:135-150).
- **Implicit: the model must find these in prose**
  - whether a review verdict is on record
  - whether work is merged, Done, or CI red (meta:143-149, 192-194)
  - whether a plan exists and plan-review is due (198-217)
  - prior plan-review verdicts (210-213)
  - whether a bug was already investigated (184-188)
  - Blocked-by relations are not in the prompt at all: `ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY` selects none at issue level (providers/linear/index.js:363-430). That is LIN-3301.
- **Not available to the router at all:**
  - dispatch and stage history
  - ledgers
  - `stateTransitions`, which are fetched (linear/index.js:947-954) but go unused
  - git, PRs and CI (meta:192 says so)
- `featureFlags` change nothing in routing mode except the tracker rename (meta:85-88 are used only inside W blocks).

**L3. Router output contract and parse (openrouter.js:1733-1834)**
- The reply is markdown, not JSON: `## Reasoning`, then Assessment, optional Signal Status, `→ **<action>**`, optional `**DeferTo:**`, and `**Next:**`.
- The action comes from a regex on the reasoning text (`parseRecommendedAction`, 1733). The defer target comes from `parseDeferTo` (1752).
- One parser serves two modes:

  | Case | Routing mode | Full mode |
  |---|---|---|
  | Missing action | throws (1814-1819) | not checked |
  | Unknown action | throws "names no stage" (`composeRoutedRecommendation`, 2162) | becomes `custom` and the prompt still ships (`deriveDispatchKind`, prompt-templates.js:232) |

- There is no retry and no confidence field.
- **Defects found, both confirmed by running the code:**
  - **D1, live reasoning lost.** `StreamingSectionParser` only starts on `## Reasoning\n` (openrouter.js:888). The routing-mode parse accepts `**Reasoning**`, a form seen live (1785, commit `2c5383d5`). Fed `**Reasoning**\n…→ **plan**`, the stream parser emits **0 events**, while the final parse returns `plan`. The `done` event carries no reasoning (1207). So on the true-streaming UI path the live reasoning, with the chosen stage in it, is probably never shown. That last step is inferred, not tested in the UI.
  - **D2, out-of-list stage accepted.** The router accepts a stage outside its list. `→ **retro**` parses as `retro` even though `retro` is deliberately excluded (prompt-templates.js:427). Because `PROMPT_TEMPLATES.retro` exists, it would then be written as a retro prompt. That last step is inferred.

**L4. Composition after the choice (openrouter.js:2158-2164; brief-writer.js)**
- The action becomes a kind, then `writeStagePrompt(kind, …)` builds the prompt, with the writer's focus set to `routerFocus` (2011).
  - `routerFocus` keeps only the `→` and `**Next:**` lines.
  - The Assessment is deliberately withheld, because of the `copied-router` guard.
- Writer failures never throw; the unwritten body ships. Defers skip the writer.

**L5. Model and budgets**
- **Router model:** `resolveAiOperationModel({opKind:'recommend'})`, which checks `byKind.recommend`, then `prefs.modelId`, then `DEFAULT_MODEL = openai/gpt-5.4-mini` (brief-writer.js:83; workspace-preferences.js:229-242; openrouter.js:28). The free tier is clamped (openrouter.js:317-322).
- **Token budget:** `RECOMMENDATION_MAX_TOKENS = 8000` (openrouter.js:125) applies in routing mode too, although the reply is a few hundred tokens. It is set alongside the writer's budget and the descent timeouts in proxy.js:373-392 and workspace-api.js:33-38 (LIN-3297).

**L6. Every path that triggers or consumes the choice.** The full list is in the class list below. Bound: both entry points (`getRecommendation` at openrouter.js:2166 and `getRecommendationStream` at 961) and the 11 `createDispatchItem` sites.
- **Routed surfaces:**
  - UI stream (workspace-api.js:1155)
  - UI buffered (:918)
  - proxy GET recommend (proxy-compute.js:356)
  - recommend-and-dispatch (proxy-dispatch.js:740)
  - All four go through the descent `resolveRecommendation` (recommend-recurse.js:106), and all honour the writer (`resolveRecommendModels`, brief-writer.js:82).
- **Consumers of the output:**
  - The descent reads `recommendedAction` and `deferTo` (recurse:165, 178-201).
  - Proxy JSON returns `recommendedAction` and `kind` (proxy-compute.js:551).
  - recommend-and-dispatch sets `effectiveKind`, which drives the duplicate guard and per-kind defaults (proxy-dispatch.js:1315, 1439; dispatch-factory.js:358, 420-460).
  - The UI renders the reasoning text raw (public/prompt-section.js:743-785).
  - Neither UI JSON nor the SSE `done` event returns the action or kind (workspace-api.js:1093-1105, 1440).
- **D3 (cited by an agent, not re-run by me).** A stage chosen with the UI "✦ next step" button is dispatched as `promptName: 'AI Recommendation'` with no `kind`, so it is stored as `custom` (prompt-section.js:995; prompt-templates.js:232).

**L7. Stages set without the router (pinned or fixed)**
- UI stage buttons (workspace-api.js:474)
- proxy `?kind=` (proxy-compute.js:417-502)
- recommend-and-dispatch with `kind` (proxy-dispatch.js:929-1211)
- the proxy template read (proxy-compute.js:283, which ignores the writer)
- feedback triage (workspace-api.js ~3713/3735)
- the close-out press (public/session.js:807-822)
- fixed kinds: autopilot, wake, follow-up
- The only persistent mark of a pinned stage is the proxy-events endpoint tag `(override:<kind>)` (proxy-dispatch.js:1149).

**L8. Parallel deciders: agents choosing the next stage in prose**
- Autopilot pins a stage when it judges the engine wrong (autopilot-kickoff.js:508-526, 584-593; docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md:157-168).
- Others: worker lane (docs/worker-lane-prompt.md:5), passage runner and planner, and Flight Companion (flight-companion-kickoff.js:126).
- These are the router's main *correction* signal and its main *consumer*. A change to the router's vocabulary or output must stay consistent with their prose.

**L9. Stage vocabulary**
- Source of truth: `PROMPT_TEMPLATES` with an `aiHint` minus `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION`, plus `RECOMMEND_META_ACTIONS=['defer']` (prompt-templates.js:427-453).
- Live list, 17 entries: blocked, bug, plan, look into, triage, breakdown, research, scoping, design, spike, context, plan-review, implement, review, close-out, retrospective-audit, defer.
- **Mirrors:**
  - meta:67 fallback
  - the decision-tree prose, which mixes `implement` and `implementation`
  - `STAGE_LEADS` (prompt-template-defs.js:70-88)
  - `STAGE_INTENT` and `PROCESS_ONLY` (prompts/brief-writer.js:4-35)
  - `COMPLETION_SIGNALS` (completion-signals.js:31-225)
  - `CONTRACT_LINES`, `VIRTUAL_PROMPTS` (workflow-config.js:24-40), `DISPATCH_KINDS`
  - the autopilot prose (autopilot-kickoff.js:512)

**L10. Measurement as it stands**
- **LIN-3107 harness** (`scripts/eval/jev-routing-eval.mjs`, `09241ba1`, `1dffc408`):
  - 66 fixtures, about 26 from real tickets and the rest synthetic or constructed.
  - Scoring is set membership in `expect`. 26 of 66 accept more than one answer; `avoid` exists on only 10 cases and is reported but does not change the score.
  - Live arm: 79.1% at K=5 with gpt-5.4-mini. Run to run it varies by about 3 points (stability.md:14-40).
  - **It calls `getRecommendation` without `briefWriter` (eval.mjs:364). It measures the full choose-and-write prompt, not the routing-only call that is live in John's workspace.**
- **Other harnesses:**
  - `eval-research-routing.mjs` with `regen-baseline.mjs` snapshots the full prompt only (regen-baseline.mjs:20-30).
  - `eval-recommend-baseline.mjs` also runs without the writer (:103).
  - `brief-writer-compare.mjs` (LIN-3294) is the **only** script that runs routing-only (`briefWriter: {model}, deadline: 0`, :271). It records each route but never grades it.
- **Does the metric track the real outcome? No, not yet.** It can read green while routing is wrong:
  1. It doesn't run the live path.
  2. It treats wrong and suboptimal alike; any answer outside the set is an equal miss. LIN-3107's own research warned of this.
  3. It isn't weighted to real failures. In a census of real misses (about 105 among 3,057 issues), 72 were landed work routed to implement or close-out instead of review, and only a handful of fixtures cover that.
  4. It grades only the action word, not the `Next:` line that now steers the writer.
- **LIN-3300's "18 of 24 vs 16" and the LIN-3140 "routing notes":** no source found in Linear, the repo, git or local scratchpads.

**L11. Persisted production record**
- **prompt-traces** (prompt-trace-store.js:21-40, 160-190; lifetime retention since `c572a681`) stores per hop:
  - the full `metaPrompt`, which freezes exactly what the router saw
  - `rawContent` and `reasoning`
  - the writer outcome
- **What prompt-traces lacks:**
  - a parsed action, kind or deferTo field
  - a dispatch id or descent id
  - a trace for any pinned path
  - a proxy read: it is session-auth only
  - Also, `listTraces` drops `briefWriter` (:235-251).
- **dispatch-history** has `kind` and `promptName` but **no routed-or-pinned marker**. LIN-3140's rows show this: research, implementation, review and close-out have no provenance field (checked via the proxy).
- **llm-call-log** holds metadata only.
- Rows before about late August aged out under the old 30-day expiry. How much routing-only traffic exists since 3 Oct is **unverified**, because reading it needs a session.

### History
- **LIN-431 (June)** diagnosed the cause this ticket names: "variance in the prose leaks into the routing" (docs/recommendation-engine-redesign.md:67-71).
  - It proposed a separate routing call "eval'd — and voted/ensembled — on its own" (:113-116).
  - Only the facts seam shipped (`c2cb16e4`, LIN-434); the split was "not triggered" (LIN-436, :277-283).
  - The lesson it recorded is the one this ticket repeats: the measurement tool must exist before the first behaviour change, and no task should both preserve and change behaviour (:215-218).
- **Every routing failure since has been fixed by a prompt patch:**
  - research skipped (`2fed9206`)
  - over-planning (`b977581d`)
  - looping on implementation (`186d647a`)
  - stuck in review (`fdd3317a`)
  - design never chosen (`63df9ab6`)
  - plan-review gate (`7f1efdb8`)
  - re-planning approved children (`380fbf39`)
- docs/recommender-failure-patterns.md:151-160 warns against exactly that pattern.
- **LIN-3292/3293 (3-4 Oct)** added routing-only (`c84cdbfa`, `2c5383d5`), but no commit measured routing accuracy for routing-only against full mode.

### Options considered

| Option | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Measure first, on the live path, with the right metric** (recommended, step 1) | It is what the ticket demands, and it reuses existing harnesses and stored traces. | Fixtures need relabelling into wrong vs acceptable. |
| **B. Give the router its own seam** (recommended, step 2): a router prompt builder, output contract and parser in one module returning a structured decision; the full template composes its routing sections so the writer-off path stays byte-identical until LIN-3300 | It removes the cause (L1, L3), gives the eval and both entry points one thing to call, and makes LIN-3300 a deletion. | It touches the prompt-size-budget test and the baseline snapshot; equivalence must be shown byte for byte. |
| **C. JSON output from the router** | Strict parsing. | It changes behaviour (model, format) before a baseline exists. Defer it until after A. |
| **D. Change routing now** (relations, structured facts, model) | | Unmeasured. Each of these is a separate, measured follow-up (LIN-3301 and others). |

### Feasibility spike
- **Confirmed by running code:** D1 and D2 above.
- **Confirmed by reading code:**
  - The routing-only call can run alone without paying for the writer: `deadline: 0` skips it, as brief-writer-compare.mjs:271 already does.
  - The trace's `metaPrompt` is a replayable input.
- **Not run here:** an end-to-end harness run (needs an OpenRouter key) and a trace export (needs session auth).

### Closing the set
- **Searches run:**
  - `getRecommendation`, `resolveRecommendation`, `composeRoutedRecommendation`, `writeStagePrompt`, `createDispatchItem`
  - `recommendedAction`, `parseRecommendedAction`, `nextStage`, `next stage`, `routingOnly`, `prompt-traces`
  - `public/*.js` for `recommend` and `__ai__`
  - the sibling `simple-dispatcher` repo: it uses recommend only in its system-test harness (`test/system/harness/harbour.js`)
- **Checked and excluded:** observer, scheduler, periodicals and `next-run.js`. None of them choose a stage (observer-pass.js:13-20; periodicals.js:37-39; next-run.js:8-10).
- **The set would be wrong if** another repo calls `/recommend*` in production, or an agent prompt outside `lib/prompts` and `docs/` parses `recommendedAction`. Both are unlikely given the searches, but external API consumers can't be bounded from source.

### Surface Assessment
**Surface Assessment: [refactor required: move the routing half of `meta-prompt-template.js` and the routing parse into one router module (for example `lib/stage-router.js`: `buildRouterPrompt` + `parseRouteDecision` + `routeStage()` returning `{action, kind, deferTo, next, assessment, reasoning}`). Both `getRecommendation*` call it, and the full template composes the same routing sections byte-identically — reason: it removes this task's confirmed cause and is called by this task's eval arm.]**

- **Cause-or-consumer test**
  - Cause: routing-only is a subtractive mask over the writing template (meta:81). One parser serves two modes with different rules for an unknown action (openrouter.js:1774-1834 vs 2162). Writing text sits in the routing half (meta:183).
  - Consumer: step 1's routing-only eval arm and the trace annotation both call `routeStage`/`parseRouteDecision`.
- **Who-pays test**

  | Consumer | Role | Effect |
  |---|---|---|
  | `getRecommendation` / `getRecommendationStream` | beneficiary | simpler |
  | The four routed surfaces and the descent | unchanged | they consume the same `parsed` shape |
  | Writer-off full path | bystander | new obligation: byte-identical output, already pinned by `prompt-size-budget` and `meta-prompt.baseline.txt`; no runtime cost |
  | Eval harnesses | beneficiary | |

  No unjustified tax.
- This is not a second representation: the decision object *is* today's `parsed` object (openrouter.js:1814-1819) with the fields the parser already reads, given one owner.

**Scope for this ticket (John, 4 Oct):** a plain refactor. Move the next-stage choice into its own place behind one clear function, with behaviour unchanged, and point the existing routing evals at it.

The research is good. Its measurement work, the definition of wrong versus suboptimal routes, the two defects (`**Reasoning**` blanking the stream, `retro` being accepted) and any prompt or behaviour change all come later, as their own step, once the choice is isolated. Pin today's routing prompts byte for byte before moving anything, so "unchanged" is proven, not argued.

**2. "Writer-off" is inverted throughout the new prose (inside: this ticket's own docs and comments).**
Routing-only is the **writer-on** path: `const writer = options.briefWriter ? … : null; buildMetaPrompt(…, !!writer)` (`openrouter.js:2166-2169`). The new text says the opposite in 8 places:
- the `stage-router.js` header (twice)
- the `routerFragments` doc
- the `buildRouterPrompt` doc
- the `parseRouteDecision` doc
- `docs/architecture/source-map.md`
- the `brief-writer-compare.mjs` header
- the `jev-routing-eval.mjs` header
- the stage-router test header

The PR body says "writer-on" correctly. The ticket's distilled brief has already picked up "writer-off router prompt". Fix: replace "writer-off" with "writer-on" (routing-only) in each of these.

Arm 3 calls `getRecommendation(…, { featureFlags: {} })` with no `briefWriter` (`jev-routing-eval.mjs:366`). So it runs the full prompt and the full-mode `parseRecommendationResponse`. It never goes through `buildRouterPrompt` or `routeStage`; it only shares the moved fragments and `parseRecommendedAction`.

The class is "a routing-only prompt built outside `buildMetaPromptTemplate` skips that function's post-processing". `buildRouterPrompt` is its only member: no other caller builds a meta prompt outside the template (I grepped `buildRouterPrompt|buildMetaPromptTemplate|routerFragments`).
