issue.title: Give the next-stage choice a place of its own
issue.description:
Harbour chooses which stage a ticket needs next inside the meta call, the call that used to write the whole prompt. Since LIN-3299, code assembles the prompt, so choosing the stage is that call's main remaining job. But the choice is still tangled up with the old prompt-writing half. That makes it hard to see what the choice is based on, what it hands to the next stage, or how good it is.

The first live run of the new prompts (LIN-3140, 4 Oct; summary on LIN-3289) went well inside each stage. What slipped were judgements about the next step.

The aim is to make the next-stage choice its own clear, measured piece: something that can be improved and trusted on its own, leaving the rest of the prompt path simpler. A wrong route matters; a suboptimal one is fine.

Every recommendation passes through this choice, so measure before changing how it behaves.

Related: LIN-3300, LIN-3301.

parent.title: Split prompt assembly from prompt writing, and let agents fix at the cause

comments.body:
## Research notes: LIN-3304, the next-stage choice (4 Oct, HEAD `75b5c924`)

**Staleness check.** Nothing under `lib/`, `routes/`, `scripts/` or `docs/` has changed on `origin/main` since the ticket was created (10:43). The ticket's claims still hold at HEAD.

### The questions this research answered
1. What does the choice read, and how much of that is implicit?
2. What does it hand on, and to whom?
3. Where is it still tangled with prompt-writing?
4. Can it be measured today, and would the measurement track a *wrong* route?
5. What was tried before?

---

### Per-layer audit

**L1. Router prompt (`lib/prompts/meta-prompt-template.js`)**
- Routing-only mode is not a prompt of its own. It is the full template with the writing blocks blanked: `const W = (text) => routingOnly ? '' : text;` (meta:81). It only removes text; nothing is added.
- **Routing sections, kept in both modes:**
  - facts (96-104)
  - role (106)
  - Task Context (110)
  - Sequential Workflow Decision with Steps 0-4 (128-240)
  - Action Types Reference (308-312) and Completion Signals (313-321)
  - instructions 1-2 (333-335)
  - reply skeleton (338-348) and action/DeferTo rules (352-354)
- **Writing sections, W-gated:** 113-127, 132, 241-307 (about 60 KB of quality rules), 322-332, 336, 349-351, 355.
- **Size**, with empty issue context:

  | Case | Routing-only | Full |
  |---|---|---|
  | Leaf | 41.6 KB | 103 KB |
  | Node | 49 KB | 111 KB |

  The issue context is unbounded on top of that: the full description and every comment (openrouter.js:623-636, 759-763).
- **Writing text left inside the routing half:**
  - meta:183 says "the generated prompt should skip full analysis", about a prompt this call no longer writes.
  - meta:143-144 say what review and close-out *write*.
  - meta:239 restates the defer no-body rule.
- **Trail-shaping rules** sit in the W half: plan-review due, session fit, the verdict format, "name the next action" (meta:132, 293, 298-304). The router reads these back later. Routing-only still works because code now owns them: `lib/prompt-contract.js` carries `plan-review due` and `Plan Review Verdict`, and `prompt-template-defs.js` carries session fit and next stage. I checked these by grep.

**L2. Router inputs (`buildMetaPrompt`, openrouter.js:784-841; `formatIssueContext`, 646-775)**
- Everything reaches the model as one prose user message at temperature 0 (openrouter.js:2211-2216). There is no structured input.
- **Explicit, computed by code:**
  - child counts, `isTerminal`, `hasOpenChildren`, and frontier facts with `nextChild` (`assembleNodeFacts`, recommendation-facts.js:89-101)
  - `sessionFit`, pulled from the description by regex (recommendation-facts.js:47-52)
  - the focused child, from `selectFocusSubtask` (tree.js:249-297)
  - Code also picks which Step 0 variant the model sees (meta:135-150).
- **Implicit: the model must find these in prose**
  - whether a review verdict is on record
  - whether work is merged, Done, or CI red (meta:143-149, 192-194)
  - whether a plan exists and plan-review is due (198-217)
  - prior plan-review verdicts (210-213)
  - whether a bug was already investigated (184-188)
  - Blocked-by relations are not in the prompt at all: `ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY` selects none at issue level (providers/linear/index.js:363-430). That is LIN-3301.
- **Not available to the router at all:**
  - dispatch and stage history
  - ledgers
  - `stateTransitions`, which are fetched (linear/index.js:947-954) but go unused
  - git, PRs and CI (meta:192 says so)
- `featureFlags` change nothing in routing mode except the tracker rename (meta:85-88 are used only inside W blocks).

**L3. Router output contract and parse (openrouter.js:1733-1834)**
- The reply is markdown, not JSON: `## Reasoning`, then Assessment, optional Signal Status, `→ **<action>**`, optional `**DeferTo:**`, and `**Next:**`.
- The action comes from a regex on the reasoning text (`parseRecommendedAction`, 1733). The defer target comes from `parseDeferTo` (1752).
- One parser serves two modes:

  | Case | Routing mode | Full mode |
  |---|---|---|
  | Missing action | throws (1814-1819) | not checked |
  | Unknown action | throws "names no stage" (`composeRoutedRecommendation`, 2162) | becomes `custom` and the prompt still ships (`deriveDispatchKind`, prompt-templates.js:232) |

- There is no retry and no confidence field.
- **Defects found, both confirmed by running the code:**
  - **D1, live reasoning lost.** `StreamingSectionParser` only starts on `## Reasoning\n` (openrouter.js:888). The routing-mode parse accepts `**Reasoning**`, a form seen live (1785, commit `2c5383d5`). Fed `**Reasoning**\n…→ **plan**`, the stream parser emits **0 events**, while the final parse returns `plan`. The `done` event carries no reasoning (1207). So on the true-streaming UI path the live reasoning, with the chosen stage in it, is probably never shown. That last step is inferred, not tested in the UI.
  - **D2, out-of-list stage accepted.** The router accepts a stage outside its list. `→ **retro**` parses as `retro` even though `retro` is deliberately excluded (prompt-templates.js:427). Because `PROMPT_TEMPLATES.retro` exists, it would then be written as a retro prompt. That last step is inferred.

**L4. Composition after the choice (openrouter.js:2158-2164; brief-writer.js)**
- The action becomes a kind, then `writeStagePrompt(kind, …)` builds the prompt, with the writer's focus set to `routerFocus` (2011).
  - `routerFocus` keeps only the `→` and `**Next:**` lines.
  - The Assessment is deliberately withheld, because of the `copied-router` guard.
- Writer failures never throw; the unwritten body ships. Defers skip the writer.

**L5. Model and budgets**
- **Router model:** `resolveAiOperationModel({opKind:'recommend'})`, which checks `byKind.recommend`, then `prefs.modelId`, then `DEFAULT_MODEL = openai/gpt-5.4-mini` (brief-writer.js:83; workspace-preferences.js:229-242; openrouter.js:28). The free tier is clamped (openrouter.js:317-322).
- **Token budget:** `RECOMMENDATION_MAX_TOKENS = 8000` (openrouter.js:125) applies in routing mode too, although the reply is a few hundred tokens. It is set alongside the writer's budget and the descent timeouts in proxy.js:373-392 and workspace-api.js:33-38 (LIN-3297).

**L6. Every path that triggers or consumes the choice.** The full list is in the class list below. Bound: both entry points (`getRecommendation` at openrouter.js:2166 and `getRecommendationStream` at 961) and the 11 `createDispatchItem` sites.
- **Routed surfaces:**
  - UI stream (workspace-api.js:1155)
  - UI buffered (:918)
  - proxy GET recommend (proxy-compute.js:356)
  - recommend-and-dispatch (proxy-dispatch.js:740)
  - All four go through the descent `resolveRecommendation` (recommend-recurse.js:106), and all honour the writer (`resolveRecommendModels`, brief-writer.js:82).
- **Consumers of the output:**
  - The descent reads `recommendedAction` and `deferTo` (recurse:165, 178-201).
  - Proxy JSON returns `recommendedAction` and `kind` (proxy-compute.js:551).
  - recommend-and-dispatch sets `effectiveKind`, which drives the duplicate guard and per-kind defaults (proxy-dispatch.js:1315, 1439; dispatch-factory.js:358, 420-460).
  - The UI renders the reasoning text raw (public/prompt-section.js:743-785).
  - Neither UI JSON nor the SSE `done` event returns the action or kind (workspace-api.js:1093-1105, 1440).
- **D3 (cited by an agent, not re-run by me).** A stage chosen with the UI "✦ next step" button is dispatched as `promptName: 'AI Recommendation'` with no `kind`, so it is stored as `custom` (prompt-section.js:995; prompt-templates.js:232).

**L7. Stages set without the router (pinned or fixed)**
- UI stage buttons (workspace-api.js:474)
- proxy `?kind=` (proxy-compute.js:417-502)
- recommend-and-dispatch with `kind` (proxy-dispatch.js:929-1211)
- the proxy template read (proxy-compute.js:283, which ignores the writer)
- feedback triage (workspace-api.js ~3713/3735)
- the close-out press (public/session.js:807-822)
- fixed kinds: autopilot, wake, follow-up
- The only persistent mark of a pinned stage is the proxy-events endpoint tag `(override:<kind>)` (proxy-dispatch.js:1149).

**L8. Parallel deciders: agents choosing the next stage in prose**
- Autopilot pins a stage when it judges the engine wrong (autopilot-kickoff.js:508-526, 584-593; docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md:157-168).
- Others: worker lane (docs/worker-lane-prompt.md:5), passage runner and planner, and Flight Companion (flight-companion-kickoff.js:126).
- These are the router's main *correction* signal and its main *consumer*. A change to the router's vocabulary or output must stay consistent with their prose.

**L9. Stage vocabulary**
- Source of truth: `PROMPT_TEMPLATES` with an `aiHint` minus `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION`, plus `RECOMMEND_META_ACTIONS=['defer']` (prompt-templates.js:427-453).
- Live list, 17 entries: blocked, bug, plan, look into, triage, breakdown, research, scoping, design, spike, context, plan-review, implement, review, close-out, retrospective-audit, defer.
- **Mirrors:**
  - meta:67 fallback
  - the decision-tree prose, which mixes `implement` and `implementation`
  - `STAGE_LEADS` (prompt-template-defs.js:70-88)
  - `STAGE_INTENT` and `PROCESS_ONLY` (prompts/brief-writer.js:4-35)
  - `COMPLETION_SIGNALS` (completion-signals.js:31-225)
  - `CONTRACT_LINES`, `VIRTUAL_PROMPTS` (workflow-config.js:24-40), `DISPATCH_KINDS`
  - the autopilot prose (autopilot-kickoff.js:512)

**L10. Measurement as it stands**
- **LIN-3107 harness** (`scripts/eval/jev-routing-eval.mjs`, `09241ba1`, `1dffc408`):
  - 66 fixtures, about 26 from real tickets and the rest synthetic or constructed.
  - Scoring is set membership in `expect`. 26 of 66 accept more than one answer; `avoid` exists on only 10 cases and is reported but does not change the score.
  - Live arm: 79.1% at K=5 with gpt-5.4-mini. Run to run it varies by about 3 points (stability.md:14-40).
  - **It calls `getRecommendation` without `briefWriter` (eval.mjs:364). It measures the full choose-and-write prompt, not the routing-only call that is live in John's workspace.**
- **Other harnesses:**
  - `eval-research-routing.mjs` with `regen-baseline.mjs` snapshots the full prompt only (regen-baseline.mjs:20-30).
  - `eval-recommend-baseline.mjs` also runs without the writer (:103).
  - `brief-writer-compare.mjs` (LIN-3294) is the **only** script that runs routing-only (`briefWriter: {model}, deadline: 0`, :271). It records each route but never grades it.
- **Does the metric track the real outcome? No, not yet.** It can read green while routing is wrong:
  1. It doesn't run the live path.
  2. It treats wrong and suboptimal alike; any answer outside the set is an equal miss. LIN-3107's own research warned of this.
  3. It isn't weighted to real failures. In a census of real misses (about 105 among 3,057 issues), 72 were landed work routed to implement or close-out instead of review, and only a handful of fixtures cover that.
  4. It grades only the action word, not the `Next:` line that now steers the writer.
- **LIN-3300's "18 of 24 vs 16" and the LIN-3140 "routing notes":** no source found in Linear, the repo, git or local scratchpads.

**L11. Persisted production record**
- **prompt-traces** (prompt-trace-store.js:21-40, 160-190; lifetime retention since `c572a681`) stores per hop:
  - the full `metaPrompt`, which freezes exactly what the router saw
  - `rawContent` and `reasoning`
  - the writer outcome
- **What prompt-traces lacks:**
  - a parsed action, kind or deferTo field
  - a dispatch id or descent id
  - a trace for any pinned path
  - a proxy read: it is session-auth only
  - Also, `listTraces` drops `briefWriter` (:235-251).
- **dispatch-history** has `kind` and `promptName` but **no routed-or-pinned marker**. LIN-3140's rows show this: research, implementation, review and close-out have no provenance field (checked via the proxy).
- **llm-call-log** holds metadata only.
- Rows before about late August aged out under the old 30-day expiry. How much routing-only traffic exists since 3 Oct is **unverified**, because reading it needs a session.

### History
- **LIN-431 (June)** diagnosed the cause this ticket names: "variance in the prose leaks into the routing" (docs/recommendation-engine-redesign.md:67-71).
  - It proposed a separate routing call "eval'd — and voted/ensembled — on its own" (:113-116).
  - Only the facts seam shipped (`c2cb16e4`, LIN-434); the split was "not triggered" (LIN-436, :277-283).
  - The lesson it recorded is the one this ticket repeats: the measurement tool must exist before the first behaviour change, and no task should both preserve and change behaviour (:215-218).
- **Every routing failure since has been fixed by a prompt patch:**
  - research skipped (`2fed9206`)
  - over-planning (`b977581d`)
  - looping on implementation (`186d647a`)
  - stuck in review (`fdd3317a`)
  - design never chosen (`63df9ab6`)
  - plan-review gate (`7f1efdb8`)
  - re-planning approved children (`380fbf39`)
- docs/recommender-failure-patterns.md:151-160 warns against exactly that pattern.
- **LIN-3292/3293 (3-4 Oct)** added routing-only (`c84cdbfa`, `2c5383d5`), but no commit measured routing accuracy for routing-only against full mode.

### Options considered

| Option | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Measure first, on the live path, with the right metric** (recommended, step 1) | It is what the ticket demands, and it reuses existing harnesses and stored traces. | Fixtures need relabelling into wrong vs acceptable. |
| **B. Give the router its own seam** (recommended, step 2): a router prompt builder, output contract and parser in one module returning a structured decision; the full template composes its routing sections so the writer-off path stays byte-identical until LIN-3300 | It removes the cause (L1, L3), gives the eval and both entry points one thing to call, and makes LIN-3300 a deletion. | It touches the prompt-size-budget test and the baseline snapshot; equivalence must be shown byte for byte. |
| **C. JSON output from the router** | Strict parsing. | It changes behaviour (model, format) before a baseline exists. Defer it until after A. |
| **D. Change routing now** (relations, structured facts, model) | | Unmeasured. Each of these is a separate, measured follow-up (LIN-3301 and others). |

### Feasibility spike
- **Confirmed by running code:** D1 and D2 above.
- **Confirmed by reading code:**
  - The routing-only call can run alone without paying for the writer: `deadline: 0` skips it, as brief-writer-compare.mjs:271 already does.
  - The trace's `metaPrompt` is a replayable input.
- **Not run here:** an end-to-end harness run (needs an OpenRouter key) and a trace export (needs session auth).

### Closing the set
- **Searches run:**
  - `getRecommendation`, `resolveRecommendation`, `composeRoutedRecommendation`, `writeStagePrompt`, `createDispatchItem`
  - `recommendedAction`, `parseRecommendedAction`, `nextStage`, `next stage`, `routingOnly`, `prompt-traces`
  - `public/*.js` for `recommend` and `__ai__`
  - the sibling `simple-dispatcher` repo: it uses recommend only in its system-test harness (`test/system/harness/harbour.js`)
- **Checked and excluded:** observer, scheduler, periodicals and `next-run.js`. None of them choose a stage (observer-pass.js:13-20; periodicals.js:37-39; next-run.js:8-10).
- **The set would be wrong if** another repo calls `/recommend*` in production, or an agent prompt outside `lib/prompts` and `docs/` parses `recommendedAction`. Both are unlikely given the searches, but external API consumers can't be bounded from source.

### Surface Assessment
**Surface Assessment: [refactor required: move the routing half of `meta-prompt-template.js` and the routing parse into one router module (for example `lib/stage-router.js`: `buildRouterPrompt` + `parseRouteDecision` + `routeStage()` returning `{action, kind, deferTo, next, assessment, reasoning}`). Both `getRecommendation*` call it, and the full template composes the same routing sections byte-identically — reason: it removes this task's confirmed cause and is called by this task's eval arm.]**

- **Cause-or-consumer test**
  - Cause: routing-only is a subtractive mask over the writing template (meta:81). One parser serves two modes with different rules for an unknown action (openrouter.js:1774-1834 vs 2162). Writing text sits in the routing half (meta:183).
  - Consumer: step 1's routing-only eval arm and the trace annotation both call `routeStage`/`parseRouteDecision`.
- **Who-pays test**

  | Consumer | Role | Effect |
  |---|---|---|
  | `getRecommendation` / `getRecommendationStream` | beneficiary | simpler |
  | The four routed surfaces and the descent | unchanged | they consume the same `parsed` shape |
  | Writer-off full path | bystander | new obligation: byte-identical output, already pinned by `prompt-size-budget` and `meta-prompt.baseline.txt`; no runtime cost |
  | Eval harnesses | beneficiary | |

  No unjustified tax.
- This is not a second representation: the decision object *is* today's `parsed` object (openrouter.js:1814-1819) with the fields the parser already reads, given one owner.

**Scope for this ticket (John, 4 Oct):** a plain refactor. Move the next-stage choice into its own place behind one clear function, with behaviour unchanged, and point the existing routing evals at it.

The research is good. Its measurement work, the definition of wrong versus suboptimal routes, the two defects (`**Reasoning**` blanking the stream, `retro` being accepted) and any prompt or behaviour change all come later, as their own step, once the choice is isolated. Pin today's routing prompts byte for byte before moving anything, so "unchanged" is proven, not argued.

issue.title: Share link: one run, one URL, readable by whoever holds it
issue.description:
**Child of milestone 4 in the v1 epic. Blocked until the sketches conversation is Done.**

## What this is

One run, one URL, readable by whoever holds it, like a CI pipeline link. The owner can turn it off. It opens without signing in, passes the public-pages secret scan, and no feedback row on it carries the repo's own content.

A shared run is how the next person arrives: the papers found that a colleague's run in front of you predicts a first agent run better than anything about you.

## What Done looks like

A run URL that returns 200 to a signed-out browser, shows the finished run as the PR display shows it, and passes `npm run scan:public-pages`.

## Read first

The sketches conversation. `docs/v1.md`, step 8 of the golden path. `lib/kpi-stats.js` for the existing privacy boundary on a public page; `npm run scan:public-pages` for the scan.

## Update from the LIN-2947 sketches sitting (26 Sep 2026)

**One page, two kinds of viewer: no separate share page.** The share link opens the run page (LIN-2948) in guest mode, on **LIN-3073's mechanism** (unguessable `/s/<token>`, owner can list and revoke, cached snapshot). Guest mode: no actions (close-out, chat, ruling answers); nothing behind the clicks (prompts, transcripts, comments, diffs; the PR link is shown and opens only with repo access); cost hidden. Ledger text shown as it is on the page; no per-field options in v1. Guards: the secret scan runs on the rendered guest view, and the owner previews ("view as guest") before sharing. A running run's link updates as it goes, then settles into the record. Future sharing (teammates, orgs) becomes more guest modes on the same page.

## Research findings (LIN-2950 research, 2026-10-03)

Grounded at `LinearViewer` HEAD `325064ee`. Research only; no code. Foundations: `docs/v1.md` step 8 (`:50`), the share rule (`:74`), the gaps row (`:115`); LIN-2947 (Q1/Q5/Q8); `lib/kpi-stats.js` (public-page boundary — counts + app labels only, `:1-30`); `npm run scan:public-pages` (`scripts/scan-public-pages.mjs` → `lib/scan-public-pages.js`).

### Recommended approach for the plan

1. **Integration seam: A — a stored guest-run snapshot, reusing the LIN-3073 store/token/matrix/TTL/backoff/limiters/exemptions/headers.** Add a `run` subject; a GET-triggered refresh reconstructs the session through a **new injected reader** (mirroring `createReadOwnerIssues`, `lib/share-owner-reader.js:33`) and stores a **strict guest projection**. `/s/:token` renders that snapshot. This satisfies the cache contract (an anonymous viewer never triggers a live provider read) and "updates as it goes, then settles": refresh while the session is non-terminal, **freeze on terminal** (stop refreshing once `sessionIsTerminal`).
2. **Renderer: a** `guest` **viewer option on** `renderSessionPage` — not a forked renderer — so there is **one** source of truth for what the page shows and guest/owner cannot drift; the strict projection (allow-list mirroring `lib/share-snapshot.js:55-65`) feeds it.
3. **Guest hide set:** actions (chat link, question cards, close-out box, reply/proposals, back-to-feed), behind-the-click (transcripts/`data-feedback`, ticket-walk outcome prose, qcard case prose, proposal prompts, brief/recap), cost, credential + peakRSS, nav/footer/app scripts, and `data-url-key`.
4. **Secret scan:** render-time fail-closed over the final guest HTML (`scanText`; the rules are token-shaped — git SHAs and PR URLs do not trip) **plus** a test-time proof. The scheduled `scan:public-pages` cannot discover `/s/<token>` and scans JS only, so the Done line is proven via `scanPublicPages({ explicitPages })` + `scanText(fullHtml)`.
5. **Owner UX:** create/list/revoke from the run page and the Settings "Share links" section (extended for the `run` kind); a **"view as guest"** preview link that renders the guest projection owner-side before sharing.

### Design: freeze, freshness and the PR-state store (B4, B5, B3)

**B4: the terminal signal can flip back.** `sessionIsTerminal` (`routes/dashboard.js:296-301`) returns the anchor loop's terminality alone when an anchor exists, so an anchored session stays "terminal" while a reply or a LIN-3254 proposal Apply runs a follow-up loop; an anchorless session flips back to non-terminal. `loopIsTerminal` is private (`:282`). Resolution: **a freeze is a revalidated cache state, not a permanent one, and there is no TTL exemption.**

* New `sessionIsSettled(session) = sessionIsTerminal(session) && every loop is terminal`, exported beside `sessionIsTerminal` (S2a). A stuck loop means "never settles", the safe direction. Injected into the share reader as a dependency, the same pattern as `server.js:470,485`; the materializer injections stay on the anchor-based gate.
* **Watermark:** `settledKey = inputHash(buildRunView(session))` (`lib/run-paragraph.js:173`): a digest of the title plus every ended loop's id, kind and terminalStatus. A follow-up loop that starts and ends between two probes still changes the key. Paragraph catch-up uses the same key (`paragraph.inputHash === settledKey`).
* **Matrix interplay (the LIN-3073 7 rows).** Rows 1–4 (token, revoked, owner, owner-check error) run first and are untouched. Row 5 (fresh under 60 s) is untouched. A due run refresh starts with a **local probe** (`loadRunLocal`: Mongo only, no tracker or GitHub read). If the stored snapshot is settled, `sessionIsSettled` is still true and the key is unchanged, it is a **revalidate**: `saveSnapshot(key, record.snapshot, {at})` bumps `snapshotAt` and the page is served with zero provider reads, under the existing `MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS`, backoff, single-flight and `readLimiter`. Otherwise it is a full refresh; a reopened run is un-frozen, renders as running, and follows the normal 60 s TTL. Rows 6 and 7 are unchanged: a probe or refresh failure serves last-good "as of" (row 6) or 503 with backoff (row 7), and the whole run path (probe, revalidate, external read, projection, scan, save) sits inside the LIN-3243 L4 try/catch (`routes/share.js` \~`:229-257`, `ad6117e1`), so a build or save failure becomes row 6 or row 7. Revoke on a frozen snapshot still returns 410 (row 2).

**B5: the freeze captures cached and async sources.** Evidence (@ `bc253bec`): the header PR state is cached up to 15 min while open (`PR_STATE_OPEN_TTL_MS`, `routes/dashboard.js:99`) and falls back to a stale value or "state not reported" when the 36/h budget is spent (`readPrState` `:1548-1568`); the evidence block's PR read goes through `readPrStatusFailOpen` (own 60 s cache, no budget, no timestamps; `lib/github-pr-status.js:235`); the paragraph is regenerated asynchronously (`lib/run-paragraph-hook.js:62-70`). Resolution: stamp each source with its own age and settle only when each is caught up.

* **One PR read per refresh.** The guest reader injects a `readPrStatus` adapter into `readRunEvidence` (the parameter already exists) backed by the shared store (S0). The header line and the evidence "now" row come from the same raw result, so they cannot disagree. The authed page is unchanged.
* The projection stores `prState: {state, number, checks, asOf}` where `asOf` is the cache entry's `fetchedAt` (null when nothing was read). The PR line and the evidence "now" row carry **their own** "as of `<fetchedAt>`"; when `asOf` is null the line shows no stamp and asserts nothing. The page-level `capturedAt` stamp remains for row-6 last-good serves.
* **Settling gate.** A snapshot is `settled` only when all hold: (a) `sessionIsSettled`; (b) the PR read is determinate: `none`, `multiple`, or a read via fresh or cache whose `fetchedAt >= lastFinishedAt` (the last step end in the run view), where a successful `readable:false` read (private or off-allowlist repo) also counts; a thrown or unavailable read, a budget-exhausted stale fallback, or a too-old cache entry is not determinate; (c) the paragraph is matched, or `now >= lastFinishedAt + PARAGRAPH_GRACE_MS` (10 min, stateless). Unsettled-but-terminal snapshots keep the normal 60 s TTL and re-read at each due refresh.
* **Paragraph.** The projection carries it only when `stored.inputHash === settledKey`, i.e. it describes exactly the steps shown; otherwise null. After the grace a run with no paragraph (offline, no key) settles without one; a paragraph generated later does not appear on that frozen snapshot until the key changes (absent, not false).
* **Budget impact.** Guest PR reads go through the shared 36/h cap and the shared `repo#number` cache. A settle may force one real read (at most 4 calls) when the cached entry predates the last step; cached merged/closed entries (24 h TTL) with `fetchedAt >= lastFinishedAt` cost nothing. Capacity is about 2 simultaneously live open PRs (36 / (4 calls x 4 per hour)); under contention the guest shows the last cached value with its true older `asOf` or "state not reported" and settling waits. This is the existing LIN-3251 cap, not new spend.

**B3: the PR-state store is closure-local.** `prStateStore` (cache, sliding 36/h bucket, allowlist cache) is built inside `createDashboardRoutes` (`routes/dashboard.js:735-743`); `readPrState` (`:1548`), the allowlist helper (`:1456`), the budget helpers (`:1508-1536`) and the route's PR-ref resolution (`:1576-1604`) are closures. Routing an outside-scope item from LIN-3254's close-out.

LIN-3254 (run-page chat proposals) reviewed to Approve. Its review's `### What CI Did Not Prove` ledger item 3 is **outside** that ticket's bounded class: the run page's "💬 chat about this run" link is rendered outside the `canReply` reply-box gate, so when guest mode suppresses actions only the proposal block is hidden while the chat link still shows. LIN-3254 intentionally gates only the proposal block (guest mode does not exist yet there).

When this ticket builds guest mode's "no actions" set, it must also hide the "💬 chat about this run" link on the run page, alongside the proposal block and the other actions. Added a `related` link LIN-3254 ↔ LIN-2950 to record it. (Review references: LIN-3254 round 1 ledger item 3 and round 2 non-blocking note 2.)

**Autopilot (stepper) — run 741edb42 started.** Next step from the engine: **research** (the first recommend returned an empty-placeholder `plan` prompt; the retry gave a real research prompt, which fits a fresh ticket whose run-page ↔ `/s/<token>` integration point is still unspecified). Stepping it as 4 beats in one warm session, ROOT dispatch `0ae5f096-1f63-49e9-acbe-160d5fd10eae`: (1) re-ground + foundations, (2) layer audit, (3) classes + adversarial self-review, (4) Surface Assessment + tracker write-up. Settled rulings passed through: lin2942-mode-on-run = link-only; lin3073-owner-unresolvable = serve-last-good. LIN-2954 out of scope.

# LIN-2950 research — exploration notes (2026-10-03)

Research only; no code, no plan. Grounded at `LinearViewer` HEAD `325064ee` (`main == origin/main`, clean). 4 beats: re-ground + foundations, layer audit, class register + self-review, this write-up.

## 1. Foundations (beat 1)

- **`docs/v1.md`** — step 8 (`:50`) "One run, one URL, readable by whoever holds it"; the share rule (`:74`) "the same page seen as a guest, at an unguessable key in the URL (the mechanism of LIN-3073): no actions, and nothing behind the clicks, meaning no prompts, transcripts, comments, diffs or cost; secret-scanned and previewed by its owner before it is sent"; gaps row (`:115`).
- **LIN-2947** (Done, 26 Sep) — Q1 run = one page per task; Q5 money shown when known, omitted never guessed; Q8 share = same page as guest, no actions, secret-scanned as rendered, owner previews.
- **`lib/kpi-stats.js`** (`:1-30`) — the public-page privacy boundary: counts + app-defined labels only, never workspace keys/content. The guest run page follows the *principle* (strict allow-list), not the literal counts-only shape.
- **`npm run scan:public-pages`** → `scripts/scan-public-pages.mjs` → `lib/scan-public-pages.js`. Fetches `/`, `/kpis`, `/archive/:n`; extracts and scans **served JS only** (`:222`); `clean = findings===0 && errors===0` (`:233`). Takes `baseUrl`/`explicitPages`/`fetchImpl` (`:115-125`) — no file/snapshot input. Ran clean at HEAD (10 pages, 11 JS assets).
- **LIN-3073 + LIN-3243 + LIN-3244 + LIN-3255** (Done) built the mechanism; ruling `lin3073-owner-unresolvable` = serve-last-good. **LIN-2948** (Done) rescoped the run page to the session page; **LIN-3247** (Done) added the ledger reader + guest-safe evidence fragments; **LIN-3254** (Done) added the chat link + proposals and routed the chat-link gate gap here.
- **Staleness:** everything referenced changed since 2026-09-19 except the scan scripts (unchanged since `6b212477`); line refs in LIN-2948's plan drifted (`routes/dashboard.js:1142→1229`, `lib/render-session.js:637→871`).

## 2. Layer audit (beat 2)

**1. Share subject + store.** Collection-only: `SUBJECT_KINDS=['parent','label']` (`routes/share.js:108`), `validSubject` requires `type:'collection'` (`lib/share-store.js:69-77`), `buildShareSnapshot` throws otherwise (`lib/share-snapshot.js:76-79`). Document shape `lib/share-store.js:111-124`; token = 32 random bytes base64url, sha256 `_id` (`:49-51,107-108`); indexes subject-generic (`lib/db-indexes.js:316-329`). Owner routes gated by `resolveOwnerMintRefusal` first (`routes/share.js:344-483`); 7-row matrix before cache (`:258-334`); refresh hardcodes the collection reader `readOwnerIssues` (`:220`). **Run ownership = the workspace owner** (the `role:'owner'` edge, `lib/account-workspace-store.js:145-148`, `lib/workspace-owner.js:66-78`), same gate as collections; refresh resolves the owner credential via `resolveWorkspaceAccess(urlKey, ownerAccountId)` (`lib/share-owner-reader.js:34-35`).

**2. Snapshot + liveness.** Loader `routes/dashboard.js:1229-1340`: `loadSessionWithTranscript` (`:1248`, def `:1542`) → `pointReadSession` (`:1565`, issue-scoped with a whole-workspace fallback `:1546`); `joinSessionIssueContext` (`:1257`, pure cache reads `:1654-1655`); `buildRunView` (`:1295`, pure, `lib/run-view.js:256`, returns `{runId,title,steps,progress,next,cost,time,waiting}` `:325-334`, raw loops embedded); `runProposalsStore.list` (`:1299`); `readRunEvidence` (`:1307`, `lib/run-evidence.js:202`); `runParagraphStore.get` (`:1313`). Feedback rows embedded via `data-feedback` (`lib/render-session.js:193-198,248-253`). Liveness: session live→terminal-stable; proposals live; PR state live while open; paragraph regenerated at step ends; brief/recap cached. "Updates as it goes, then settles" needs a subject-kind-dispatched refresh + a **terminal freeze** the collection refresh lacks.

**3. Render.** `renderSessionPage` (`lib/render-session.js:871`) always builds nav+footer (`:891-892`) and loads app scripts (`:1031`); `renderPage` always emits the inline theme script (`lib/components/page.js:28-29,95`). Action regions gated on `canReply` (`:431,446,498,501,615,652`); the chat link (`:964-965`), qcard presence (`:1020`), evidence mount (`:1017`), brief/recap (`:734-759`), back-link (`:889`) are not. `renderCloseOutBox` returns `''` when `!state.owner` (`lib/render-run-evidence.js:148`), but `viewerIsOwner` is hardcoded `true` (`routes/dashboard.js:1501`, `routes/workspace-api.js:4399`).

**4. Routing/auth/headers.** `/s/` exempt from token-refresh (`lib/root-route-exemption.js:25`) and PAT auto-login (`lib/pat-session.js:34-37`); share responses set `no-referrer`/`private,no-store`/`X-Robots-Tag:noindex` (`routes/share.js:260-262`) and render no nav (`lib/render-share.js:78-84`). A signed-out hit on the run-page URL redirects to `/` (`server.js:2244-2247`). Guest-unsafe client fetches: `public/session.js:612`, `public/common.js:773,851,871,1044`, `public/brief.js:35`, `public/recap.js:31`.

**5. Owner UX.** Settings "Share links" (`lib/render-settings.js:703-739`, `public/settings.js:219-263`) reuses the owner routes. No "view as guest" preview exists; no run-share UI.

**6. Secret scan.** `scanText` is generic (`lib/secret-scan.js:278`) but the public path feeds it **script content only** (`lib/scan-public-pages.js:222`); **nothing scans rendered HTML**. Feedback rows reach the page as `data-feedback` and `[evidence]` URLs (`routes/dashboard.js:1491-1493`); `message` is runner prose.

**7. Tests.** Share: `tests/unit/{share-store,share-snapshot,render-share,share-route,share-owner-routes,share-owner-reader,share-exemption,pat-session,db-indexes,connection-access-guard}.test.js`, e2e `share-links.spec.js` (scan proof `:230-238`), seam `routes/test.js:714`. Run page: `run-view`, `render-session`, `session-id-render-seam`, `session-run-transcript-entries`, `run-evidence{,-route}`, `render-run-evidence`, `run-ledger`, `run-paragraph{,-store,-hook}`, `run-proposals-store`, `lin-3254-*`, `loop-supersede`, `dashboard-routes`, `github-pr-status`; e2e `session-page`, `session-proposals`, `run-evidence`, `session-decision-layout`. Must stay green unedited: `loop-supersede.test.js`, the `db-indexes` parity guard, the `/s/` exemption tests, `chat-tools.test.js`.

## 3. Class register (beat 3)

**C1 guest-visible elements.** Bound: 16 `render*` functions in `lib/render-session.js` + fragments; 100 distinct `data-testid`s across `lib/render-session.js` + `lib/render-run-evidence.js`; 6 `<button>`. Members = the beat-2 element table.

**C2 action affordances.** 6 buttons (`:319-320,340-341,580-581`); textareas `:317,577`; radio `:571`; anchors `:889,965` + `render-run-evidence.js:152`; client writes `public/session.js:612`, `public/common.js:773,851,871,1044`, `public/brief.js:35`, `public/recap.js:31`. `canReply` gates reply/proposals/qcard-interactivity; **outside the gate: chat link, qcard presence, evidence mount/close-out, brief/recap + generate, back-link, transcript links**.

**C3 behind-the-click.** `data-feedback` (`:193-198,252`); hidden threads (`:315,578`); qcard case (`:555-560`); ticket-walk outcome (`lib/session-telemetry.js:266-286`); proposal prompt (`:350`); brief/recap bodies (`:724-731`).

**C4 cost.** Header `:947-949`; per-step `:460`/`fmtLoopCost:826`; `stepSummary:838-848`; `buildRunView().cost` (`lib/run-view.js:310-315`).

**C5 subject-kind switches (13).** `lib/share-store.js:43,72-73,117`; `lib/share-snapshot.js:47,77,86`; `routes/share.js:108,123,147,372,378,406`; `routes/test.js:725,730-731`; `public/settings.js:259,319`; plus collection-assuming `routes/share.js:220,240`, `lib/render-share.js:42`. Non-members (different namespace): `lib/ship-layout.js:267`, `public/ship.js:73,1153`.

**C6 `/s/` seams.** `lib/root-route-exemption.js:16-26`; `lib/pat-session.js:34-37`; `routes/share.js:105-106,165,258,315`; `server.js:2286`; `lib/render-share.js:42`.

### Resolved flags
- **Run paragraph → show.** Built only from `paragraphFacts` (`lib/run-paragraph.js:41-59`): title, progress, next, waiting, steps[{kind,status,finished,tier,iteration}], outcome, evidence; one cheap call from `buildRunView` (`:1-9`); cost excluded (`:16-18,43-51`); prompt forbids model id/price (`:27-31`); `buildRunView` returns no outcome/evidence today, so those are null. Carries the task title + step kinds — same class as the title.
- **Ticket-walk outcome line → hide (agent prose).** `lib/session-telemetry.js:266-286`.
- **Evidence/ledger → show (settled).** Text drawn from the task's review comment: `readRunLedger`→`parseRunLedger(latestReviewComment(comments))` over `provider.fetchIssueComments` (`lib/run-ledger.js:332,356,396-397`, `lib/run-evidence.js:213`). Recorded: the guest view deliberately shows text drawn from review comments.
- **Tier → show** (`tierOf`, `lib/run-view.js:73`); **peakRSS → hide** (host detail, `render-session.js:108`).
- **Issue titles/identifiers → precedented show** (`lib/share-snapshot.js:55-65`, `lib/render-share.js:62-75`).

### Self-review
- **Missed siblings:** `SUBJECT_KINDS` duplicated (`lib/share-store.js:43` + `routes/share.js:108`); test seam `routes/test.js:725,730-731`; settings client `public/settings.js:259,319`; refresh reader `routes/share.js:220`; snapshot build `:240`; `renderSharePage` collection-only.
- **Sync obligations:** index-parity guard; exemption tests; settings kind label; seed needs a session fixture; owner routes' parent-only branches (`routes/share.js:378-411`) must not run for a run.
- **Failure paths:** session-not-found → row 7 503 / row 6 last-good; workspace gone → row 3 410; revoke mid-run → row 2 410 before cache (`:275`); mid-run secret → caught at each render-time scan/refresh; refresh fails → row 6; no first snapshot → create refuses (`:398-401`).
- **Prior behaviour:** not-found callers (`routes/dashboard.js:1243,1250`); `viewerIsOwner` must become `false`; **`data-url-key` leakage** — `render-session` emits 7× (`:296,362,538,747,754,896,1014`) vs `render-share` 0.
- **Secret-scan feasibility:** `SECRET_RULES` (`lib/secret-scan.js:129-253`) are token-shaped (AKIA/`ghp_`/`lin_api_`/`sk-`/`xox`/PEM/`Bearer`/generic assignments) + entropy; **no generic 40-hex rule**, so git SHAs and PR URLs don't trip; the 43-char share token matches only behind `Bearer`/`bootstrap|proxy|working_token` (`:221-232`). So **render-time fail-closed is feasible with low false-positive risk** (strongest reading of "runs on the rendered guest view"); **test-time `scanText(fullHtml)` is the CI proof**; snapshot-write-time is a weaker complement.

## 4. Integration options considered
- **A. Stored guest-run snapshot; `/s/:token` renders a guest variant from it.** Mirrors collections; satisfies the cache contract and "settles" (freeze on terminal). *Recommended.*
- **B. Live-through: reconstruct per guest GET and render with a guest flag.** One renderer, but every anonymous GET reads the provider on the owner's credential — contradicts the LIN-3073 cache contract. Rejected.
- **C. Store rendered HTML at refresh; serve verbatim.** Cheapest/safest GET; scan on exact stored bytes; stores HTML not a model. Viable, combine with A.
- **D. A separate run-share store/route.** Rejected (`lib/share-store.js:32`: LIN-2950 reuses the record/cache/revoke).

## 5. Surface Assessment
`Surface Assessment: [refactor required: add a `run` subject to the LIN-3073 share mechanism — de-duplicate `SUBJECT_KINDS` (`lib/share-store.js:43` / `routes/share.js:108`) and generalize the collection-hardcoded refresh reader (`routes/share.js:220`), snapshot builder (`:240`) and renderer (`lib/render-share.js:42`) behind a subject-kind switch — consumer: `routes/share.js` / the new run-share reader] [improvement noticed, not required: add a `guest` viewer option to `renderSessionPage` (one source of truth; also drops the 7× `data-url-key`) — land inline/scoped, no separate subtask]`

**Autopilot step record — research done (verified), plan started.**

- Research ran as 4 beats in one warm session (ROOT `0ae5f096`): re-ground + foundations → layer audit → class register + adversarial self-review → Surface Assessment + write-up. Verified: description appended 1659→7868 with all original sections intact plus `## Research findings` and `### Recommended approach for the plan`; research comment `82a81ec3` carries the Surface Assessment; status In Progress. Spot-checked load-bearing claims against `325064ee` (ungated chat link `lib/render-session.js:964`, hardcoded `viewerIsOwner: true` `routes/dashboard.js:1501`, duplicate `SUBJECT_KINDS`, 7× `data-url-key`).
- PROVISIONAL for John (conservative security calls): peakRSS hidden in guest; render-time secret scan fails closed.
- Next step from the engine: **plan**. Stepping it as 4 beats in a fresh warm session (ROOT `b51e0ce1`). Beats are told to keep the problem statement / Done / Read first / 26 Sep update verbatim (the engine prompt said "replace the description").

**Autopilot plan step done** (planner session 741edb42, ROOT dispatch b51e0ce1): the plan is in the description under `## Implementation Plan`, appended after the original sections (which are unchanged). Grounded at `LinearViewer` `bc253bec`.

- **Strategy:** A, a `run` subject on the LIN-3073 mechanism with a stored strict guest projection, rendered at serve time by a `guest` option on `renderSessionPage` (not a wrapper renderer). Named gaps: none identified.
- **Drift found:** LIN-3251's header PR line and 60 s client poll must render statically in guest, with an "as of" stamp when the snapshot is frozen or stale.
- **Owner flag:** the authed run page is unchanged. The guest path passes `viewerIsOwner:false`, and the `readRunEvidence` library default (`lib/run-evidence.js:206`) flips to `false`; no current caller relies on it.
- **Session-fit:** **needs multiple sessions**, 2 phases. Phase 1 is the guest run link, server side (store/subject, reader, projection, refresh + terminal freeze, guest renderer, `/s` dispatch, fail-closed scan at refresh and serve, preview route). Phase 2 is the owner UX (run-page control, Settings create form). Each is mergeable on its own.
- **plan-review due: yes**, criteria (a) multi-session and (d) credential/merge-rule surface. (b) and (c) do not fire.
- **PROVISIONAL for John:** peakRSS hidden in guest; render-time secret scan fails closed; the frozen PR line carries an "as of" stamp (a PR-state-only refresh after terminal is noted as a possible future change, not in this ticket).

Ready for plan-review. Member-vs-owner close-out is routed to LIN-3248 (comment there). LIN-2954 stays out of scope.

**Autopilot step record — plan done (verified), plan-review started.**

- Plan ran as 4 beats in one session (ROOT `b51e0ce1`, claude-code): ground + strategy → surfaces/arrows/completeness/classes → owner-flag challenge + tests + session-fit + gate → write-up. One challenge sent and accepted on evidence: the plan no longer adds a workspace-owner check to the signed-in run page (that would have removed the close-out box from non-owner members — out of scope); guest passes `viewerIsOwner:false`, library default flips to `false` with no caller affected; member-vs-owner routed to LIN-3248.
- Verified: `## Implementation Plan` appended (7,868 → 31,946 chars), original text byte-identical as prefix; `needs multiple sessions` (2 phases) and `plan-review due: yes` ((a) multi-session, (d) credential/merge-rule) present once each; summary comment `e9719e08`.
- PROVISIONAL for John: peakRSS hidden; render-time scan fails closed; frozen PR line carries an "as of" stamp.
- Next step from the engine: **plan-review** — fresh session, 3 beats (ROOT `b29bd90a`), write-only.

## Plan-review (round 1) — Request Changes

Grounded at `LinearViewer` `bc253bec` (`main == origin/main`, clean; no drift past the plan SHA; ticket staleness clean — every post-creation commit on the ticket's named paths predates the research SHA `325064ee`). Verifier only: no edits to the description or plan, no status or label change, no follow-ups.

**Justification:** strategy A, the phase split's coherence, the relaxation bounds and the owner-flag flip all hold, but six blocking findings stand: two contradictions inside the plan (S3 vs S5; a PR anchor that does not exist), one unsequenced prerequisite (the PR-state reader), two unsafe sources behind the terminal freeze, and a Phase 1 that does not fit one session.

### Blocking findings

**B1. S3 and S5 disagree on how guest steps render; the C1 bound cannot be computed.**
- *Plan claims:* S3's allow-list keeps "steps (kind/status/finished/tier only)" and drops `loops`. S5 drops specific `renderRun` internals (`:461` cost, `:253` transcript, `:154` ticket-walk outcome, `:110` peakRSS), so it assumes `renderRun` still runs in guest. C1 is "fixed by S3's allow-list" and tested against "a named allow-set" of testids.
- *Code shows:* the steps body needs `step.loopCosts.map` and `renderLineageGroup(step.loops, …)` (`lib/render-session.js:997,1005`). `renderSessionPage` reads `session.*` directly (`:875`, `:917-1001`: `seedIssue`, `sessionId`, `tasksTouched`, `loops` for the credential rollup and the steps). A null `session` gives the not-found page (`:897`).
  - If `renderRun` is reused, these ungated members are handled by neither list: `data-loop-id` `:451`, `data-lineage-id` `:504`, `data-dispatched-at` `:422`, the per-run credential chip with `agentTokenLabel` `:120`, the `role="button"` toggle `:452`, the runtime, heartbeats and artifacts chips `:96-101`, the parked flag, and the ticket rows `:156-158`.
  - The header rows are also in neither list: active time, wall clock (`data-start`/`data-end`), waiting clock (`data-since`), seed, tasks touched.
  - The allow-set is never enumerated.
- *Plan must fix:*
  1. State one rendering path for guest steps, and sequence the `renderSessionPage` input-contract change it needs (rendering from the strict model, not from `session`).
  2. Enumerate the guest testid allow-set, which then becomes the C1 bound.
  3. Give every member above an explicit show or drop.

**B2. The "PR anchor" that S5 and S10 keep does not exist.**
- *Plan claims:* S5 says "The PR anchor stays"; S10 asserts the "PR line static with anchor kept".
- *Code shows:* the LIN-3251 PR line is a `<span>` holding plain `prStateCopy` text (`lib/render-session.js:976`; `lib/pr-state-copy.js:18-38` returns text). On the guest-kept fragments, the only link toward the PR is the evidence `checks ↗` link (`lib/render-run-evidence.js:64`, `…/pull/n/checks`), and it renders only when the check state is known. The only real PR anchor is the close-out box's (`:152`), which is owner-only and not mounted in guest.
- *Plan must fix:* say how the guest page meets "the PR link is shown" (a new element, or a named existing one), and correct the S5 and S10 wording to match.

**B3. Sharing "the existing cached reader and its budget" needs a refactor the plan never sequences.**
- *Plan claims:* S2's guest reader "reads PR state through the existing cached reader and its budget (never a direct GitHub call)". S2a extracts only "session read, issue context, `buildRunView`, evidence, paragraph".
- *Code shows:* `prStateStore` (cache, sliding 36/h bucket, allowlist cache) is created inside `createDashboardRoutes` (`routes/dashboard.js:735`). `readPrState` (`:1548`) and the run's PR-ref resolution are closures in that factory, and nothing is exported. A second instance built for `routes/share.js` would quietly double the "process-wide" cap.
- *Plan must fix:* sequence the prerequisite that makes one PR-state reader and budget instance reachable from the share refresh, name the line that consumes it, and pin it with a test (one budget across both callers).

**B4. The terminal freeze depends on a `sessionTerminal` signal that can flip back.**
- *Plan claims:* S4: "Once a stored run snapshot has `sessionTerminal: true`, the GET … serves it as a row-5 hit forever: no TTL expiry, no provider read."
- *Code shows:* `sessionIsTerminal` (`routes/dashboard.js:296-301`) is a derived gate for caching summaries. It means "the autopilot anchor is terminal, else every loop is terminal". A reply on a finished run, or a LIN-3254 proposal Apply (`followUpTo` = tail; `public/session.js:341,410,451`), adds a loop to the session. An anchorless session then becomes non-terminal again, but a frozen snapshot never re-reads, so it never sees that. Gate (c) says "nothing relaxes", yet the freeze removes the LIN-3073 TTL for run snapshots.
- *Plan must fix:* S4 must either name a terminal signal that cannot flip back, or handle a reopened run. Add a test for the reopen case, and restate gate (c) to name the TTL exemption and its bound.

**B5. The freeze captures cached and async-derived sources, and "as of `capturedAt`" gives them the wrong date.**
- *Plan claims:* the projection stores `prState`, read through the cached reader, plus the run paragraph. A frozen or stale line carries "as of <capturedAt>".
- *Code shows:*
  - PR state can be a cached value up to 15 min old while the PR is open (`PR_STATE_OPEN_TTL_MS`, `routes/dashboard.js:99`). With the budget spent, it serves stale data or "state not reported" (`b1464503`).
  - The run paragraph is regenerated asynchronously by the materializer, including "when the session turns terminal" (`lib/run-paragraph-hook.js:5-7`, `lib/session-materializer-precompute.js:97-99`).
  - So a snapshot frozen at the first terminal read can keep "PR #n is open", "state not reported" or a paragraph from before the last step forever. The stamp dates the snapshot, not the data. The primary GitHub read is available at freeze time.
  - Given the Done line ("shows the finished run as the PR display shows it"), this is load-bearing.
- *Plan must fix:* S4 and S5 must say what freshness the frozen PR state and paragraph need before a freeze is final (or what happens when they lack it), and make the stamp tell the truth about the data's age. Add tests for budget-exhausted and stale-cache freezes.

**B6. Phase 1 is not plausibly one session.**
- *Plan claims:* Phase 1 (S1, S2 + S2a, S3, S4, S5, S6, S7, S9, preview route, Settings list label, all unit rows, e2e) is one session.
- *Evidence:* the collection version of this mechanism took LIN-3243, LIN-3244 and the LIN-3255 fix round. Phase 1 here is about LIN-3243 plus part of LIN-3244, plus the S2a extraction (now coupled to the request, see N6), the PR-reader lift (B3), the `renderSessionPage` input-contract change (B1), and the projection, freeze, scan and preview, with around 10 unit files and the e2e. ### Non-blocking notes

### Per-check summary

4. Session-fit: **finding** (B6). Both phases are coherent; Phase 1 is oversized.

The `readRunEvidence` default flip tightens, and I verified no caller or test omits the flag. The TTL exemption is unnamed (B4, N11).

### Handoff

B5 asks only that the stamp tell the truth about the data's age.

**Autopilot step record — plan-review round 1: Request Changes (verified); plan revision started.**

**Plan revision 1 written** (`## Implementation Plan` in the description, replacing the round-1 plan); addresses plan-review round 1 (`68f79640`) B1–B6 and N2–N12. Grounded at `LinearViewer` `bc253bec` (no drift; LIN-3248 PR #1731 still open, re-ground on merge). **4 phases, `needs multiple sessions`, `plan-review due: yes`** ((a) multi-session, (c) narrowly: the settled-snapshot revalidate relaxes provider freshness, bounded by a 60 s local probe + `settledKey` + per-source `asOf`; (d) owner-credential reader and close-out/owner flag). Where each blocking finding is resolved:
- **B1** one guest render path: `guestSession()` stubs, literal 64-testid allow-set, member table (Design: B1; S3, S5b).
- **B2** PR link: validated `session-pr-link` anchor in the header line, owner view unchanged (Design: B2).

Ready for plan-review round 2.

**Autopilot step record — plan revision 1 done (verified); plan-review round 2 started.**

- Revision ran as 4 beats in a fresh session (ROOT `3b53be9b`): B4/B5/B3 → B1/B2 + N-notes → B6 re-split + surfaces/classes/tests/gate → write-up. Verified: prefix (7,870 chars: original sections + Research findings) byte-identical; `## Implementation Plan` replaced (31,946 → 55,919), round-1 plan text gone; `needs multiple sessions` (4 phases) and `plan-review due: yes` once each; summary comment `c3a5eda7`.
- PROVISIONAL for John now #1–#4: peakRSS hidden; render-time scan fails closed; PR line carries its own `fetchedAt` stamp (no PR-only refresh after settle); URL-shaped workspace keys stripped from ledger text.
- Plan-review round 2: fresh session, 3 beats (ROOT `5772bdf0`). Bound: this is the gate's second review; a second Request Changes goes to the human, not a third plan pass.

## Plan-review (round 2) — Request Changes

Grounded at `LinearViewer` `bc253bec` (the plan's SHA) and **`dedf98c6`** (current `origin/main`). `dedf98c6` is the merge of LIN-3248 PR #1731: 10 commits, 23 files, +2865/−33, and `bc253bec` is its ancestor. Verifier only: I made no description edit, no status or label change, and no follow-ups.

**Justification:** Revision 1 resolves every round-1 blocker at `bc253bec`, but two blocking findings stand. The first comes from #1731 merging before the revision was written, which the revision missed. The second is a hole in the B4 settled-key fix. Both are plan fixes; neither needs a human preference.

**Round-1 discharge:**
* **B1–B6 resolved** (checked against code, not the plan's say-so):
  * **B1:** 60 of the 64 allow-set testids exist (55 literally, 5 via `renderRow`/`anchor` arguments); the other 4 are marked new. The stub's per-loop keys cover every field that `buildRunView`, `renderRun`, `renderRunChips` and `computeSupersededLoopIds` read.
  * **B2:** the owner route at `dashboard.js:1433` passes no `prState`, so the anchor leaves the owner page unchanged.
  * **B3:** every lift cite holds. `fetchPrStatus` returns the shape `readPrStatusFailOpen` passes through.
  * **B4–B6:** see check 5 for the B4 residual.
* **N2, N3, N5, N11, N12 resolved.**
* **N6 partially resolved:** the rule is right, but its premise is stale. The drift section says "#1731 still OPEN" and "`origin/main == bc253bec`". In fact #1731 merged at 08:27Z, and Revision 1 was written at 08:40Z.

### Blocking findings

**F1. After #1731, the guest ledger silently drops the "open at merge" markers.**
* *Plan claims:* the ledger is shown as it is on the page. S3 never stores `closeOut`. The 64-testid allow-set and the absent-by-name list are complete (C1 = 100 owner testids).
* *Code shows (@ `dedf98c6`):*
  * `renderEvidence` now reads `model.closeOut.status`: `atMerge = closeOut.status ∈ {merged, partial}` (`lib/render-run-evidence.js:142`).
  * That value drives two new **ledger** testids, `run-evidence-ledger-open-at-merge` and `run-evidence-ledger-open-no-followup` (`:78-93`).
  * The plan's projection has no `closeOut`, so guest `atMerge` is always `false`. The owner page shows the markers and the guest page doesn't. Neither testid is in the 64-set or the absent list, so the subset assertion still passes, and the divergence is invisible to the plan's tests.
  * C1 at `dedf98c6` is 107 owner testids, not 100.
  * The source is authoritative and available. `deriveCloseOutState` makes `merged`/`partial` depend only on `prStatuses`, not on `owner`, `runnerReady` or `stopAt` (`lib/run-closeout-state.js:141-300`). It is computed from the same single PR read as the header `prState`, so it would carry the same `asOf`.
* *Bounding query (re-run on every later merge):* `awk '/^export function renderEvidence/,/^}/' lib/render-run-evidence.js | rg -o "model\.\w+(\.\w+)?"`
  * @ `bc253bec` → `{evidence, ledger}`.
  * @ `dedf98c6` → `{evidence, ledger, closeOut, closeOut.status}`.
* *Plan must fix:*
  1. Re-ground the drift section on `dedf98c6`.
  2. Decide one of:
     * (a) carry a minimal `closeOut: {status}` (or a precomputed `atMerge` boolean) in the S3 projection and pass it to `renderEvidence` in guest; add both ledger testids to the allow-set; add a guest test where a merged PR plus an undischarged item renders `run-evidence-ledger-open-at-merge`;
     * (b) record the drop as an explicit decision, against the settled "ledger shown as on the page" ruling, name both testids as absent, and assert their absence.
  3. Update C1 to the `dedf98c6` count.
* *Fix size:* a design decision between (a) and (b). (a) is the one that keeps the settled ruling. Once chosen, the change is small.

**R4. `settledKey` and `sessionIsSettled` disagree on what "terminal" means, so a reopened run can stay frozen with a step missing.**
* *Plan claims (B4):* `settledKey = inputHash(buildRunView(session))`, and "a follow-up loop that starts and ends between two probes still changes the key". A settled snapshot with an unchanged key is only revalidated (gate (c): "a changed `settledKey` or a non-settled session forces a full read").
* *Code shows (same at both SHAs; line numbers @ `dedf98c6`):*
  * `sessionIsSettled` is built on `loopIsTerminal` (`routes/dashboard.js:283`).
  * `loopIsTerminal` treats `agentState ∈ {complete, error}` as terminal before it reads any marker (`:91`, `:263`).
  * `gateFacts`, which `inputHash` digests, keeps only loops with `terminalStatus != null` (`lib/run-paragraph.js:157`).
  * `buildRunView` likewise renders such a loop as `running` (`lib/run-view.js:274`).
  * Refresh is GET-triggered only (`routes/share.js:20`), so "between two probes" can mean days.
  * Result: a follow-up loop that ends without a marker leaves `sessionIsSettled` true and the key unchanged. The next due refresh is a revalidate, and the public page permanently omits that step.
  * The plan's reopen test uses a loop with a marker, so it can't catch this. The named bound in (c) does not hold.
* *Plan must fix:* make the key and the settled check agree, and prove it.
  * Either derive `settledKey` from every loop the settled check counts (e.g. hash every `loopId` with its effective terminal state, not only `terminalStatus != null`),
  * or define settled as "every loop has `terminalStatus != null`".
  * Add a `share-run-refresh` case: a follow-up loop with `agentState:'complete'` and no `terminalStatus` appears between probes and forces a full refresh.
* *Fix size:* small and exactly specifiable. Either option satisfies the outcome; pick one and state it.

### Non-blocking notes
- **R1.** `<main class="sess-page" data-url-key="${encodedUrlKey}">` (`lib/render-session.js:1026`) still emits `data-url-key=""` when guest sets `urlKey=''`. That contradicts the plan's own absent-attribute assertion. Add the `<main>` attribute to the guest-gated list.
- **R2.** Member-table line numbers are off by 3–20 lines @ `bc253bec`: active time `:938`, wall `:939`, waiting `:941`, credential row ~`:961`, cost `:949`, seed `:952`, tasks `:929`. Members are named, so this is cosmetic.
- **R3.** The C1 query (`[^"$]+`) skips templated testids `session-${kind}`, `session-${kind}-generate` and `session-recap-${key}` (`render-session.js:708,749,756,758`). Name `session-brief` and `session-recap` in the absent list. The subset assertion already excludes them.
- **R5.** The paragraph match ignores the `final` flag. `lib/run-paragraph-hook.js:65` regenerates a paragraph with an unchanged hash when `!cached.final`. Correction: matched means `stored.inputHash === settledKey` **and `stored.final`**; otherwise the existing grace fallback applies. It shares R4's root cause.
- **R6.** `lastFinishedAt` names no existing field. `buildRunView` exposes only `time.wall.end` = `session.completedAt` (`lib/run-view.js:174-176`), which can predate a follow-up loop on an anchored session. Correction: define it as the max over loops of the enriched `completedAt` (`terminalCompletedAt`, else `resolvedAt`). The stub already keeps `terminalCompletedAt`.
- **R7.** The N-A count of `routes/dashboard.js` 43 doesn't match a re-run: 36 lines, 41 matches, same three files. Cosmetic.
- **N-P3** (a framing note for PROVISIONAL #3, not a re-opening). With #1731 merged, a `stopAt:'pr'` run normally settles with its PR open, and the owner then merges with the close-out press. The press adds no loop, so the key doesn't change, and the frozen guest page keeps "open, as of …". The stamp stays truthful, but #3 should present this as the main path, not an edge.

### Per-check summary
1. **Completeness:** **finding (F1).** At `bc253bec`, C1–C8 and N-A..N-F match the plan's members; only N-A's count is off (R7). At `dedf98c6`, C1 is 107 and the `closeOut.status` class is missed (F1). Free-text secrets are fairly declared un-sweepable.
2. **Strategy framing:** **holds.** "Named gaps: none identified" is honest: LIN-2950's relations are LIN-2954, which it blocks and which is out of scope, plus done or context tickets. The (c) narrowing and PROVISIONAL #3/#4 are disclosed, not a route around a gap.
3. **History signal:** **finding (F1, N6 premise).**
   * Carried: #1731's `readRunFacts`/`runnerReady`, the `readRunEvidence` parameters, the close-out `<button>`/`data-url-key`, and the LIN-3251 budget.
   * Missing: the `closeOut.status`-driven ledger markers.
   * Not needed: the `close-out-events` indexes, which are a new collection and leave the `shares` parity guard untouched.
4. **Session-fit:** **holds.**
   * Phase 1's S2a now also moves `readRunFacts` and the `facts` argument (`dashboard.js:~1411-1418,1764-1819` @ `dedf98c6`), which the plan anticipated.
   * The golden pin needs fixtures for the close-out box states, which adds test lines only.
   * All four phases are still landable on their own and one session each.
5. **Relaxation guard:** **finding (R4).**
   * The (c) bound fails for loops that end without a marker.
   * `validSubject` widening is bounded.
   * The `readRunEvidence` default flip (now `:234`) only tightens: both callers pass the flag explicitly (`dashboard.js:1772`, `workspace-api.js:4413`) and no test calls it directly at either SHA.
   * The new optional parameters are additive and fail-safe.
6. **Prerequisite-refactor necessity:** **holds.** Each prerequisite names the line that consumes it:
   * S0: the `readPrStatus` adapter, now `run-evidence.js:256`.
   * S2a: the S2/S4 probe and gate.
   * S5a: S5b and the B2 anchor.
   * The `SUBJECT_KINDS` de-dup: S1.

   The S2a carry of #1731's additions is stated. No refactor is missing.
7. **Source-of-truth:** **finding (F1, R5, R6).**
   * PR `fetchedAt`/`via` is authoritative.
   * `closeOut.status` is authoritative but not inherited (F1).
   * The paragraph's `final` flag is ignored (R5).
   * `lastFinishedAt` is undefined (R6).
   * The session read model, ledger comments and issue title are unchanged from round 1.

### Handoff
**Request Changes → back to `plan`.** Fix F1 (re-ground on `dedf98c6` and decide on carrying `closeOut.status`) and R4 (make the key and the settled check agree, with a markerless-loop test). R1, R2, R3, R5, R6, R7 and N-P3 can ride along, or go to implementation and review using the exact corrections above.

**Not re-opened:**
* The settled rulings: `lin2942-mode-on-run` = link-only; `lin3073-owner-unresolvable` = serve-last-good; the run page in guest mode on `/s/<token>` with no separate share page; the ledger shown as on the page.
* PROVISIONAL #1–#4 for John: peakRSS hidden; the render-time scan fails closed; the PR line's own `fetchedAt` stamp; URL-shaped workspace keys stripped. N-P3 is a framing note for #3 only.

**Autopilot — parked for John: plan-review round 2 returned Request Changes (`f4b6b616`). The bound stops a third plan pass without your say-so.**

**Where it stands.** research → plan → plan-review r1 (Request Changes: 6 blocking) → plan revision 1 → plan-review r2 (Request Changes: **2 blocking**, 7 non-blocking). Revision 1 is verified to resolve all six round-1 blockers. Nothing is implemented yet; status is In Progress; the description holds plan Revision 1 (grounded at `bc253bec`).

**What's blocked, and why.** Two blocking findings remain:
- **F1: drift, not a planning miss.** LIN-3248 PR #1731 merged at 08:27Z, 13 minutes before Revision 1 was written, and current main is `dedf98c6`. Since then the ledger renderer reads `closeOut.status` to show "open at merge" / "open, no follow-up" markers (`lib/render-run-evidence.js:142`). The guest projection drops `closeOut`, so the shared ledger would silently differ from the owner page. Fix: carry that one derived field into the projection, which keeps your settled "ledger shown as on the page", and add the two testids to the allow-set.
- **R4: a small consistency bug.** `settledKey` hashes only loops with a terminal marker, while `sessionIsSettled` also counts markerless `agentState ∈ {complete, error}`. A follow-up that ends without a marker leaves the frozen page missing that step. Fix: make the key and the check use the same terminal predicate, and add a markerless-loop test.
Both fixes are small and exactly specified in `f4b6b616`, along with exact corrections for the non-blocking notes (e.g. R5: paragraph match also requires `final`; R6: define `lastFinishedAt` as the max loop `terminalCompletedAt`). The trajectory is converging: 6 blockers became 2, and no new design questions came up.

**The decision.** The plan-review gate allows one revision cycle. That's used, so a further pass needs your authorisation.

**Options**
1. **Recommended: authorise one narrow revision 2** limited to F1 + R4 plus the listed non-blocking corrections and a re-ground at `dedf98c6`, then a **re-review scoped to those deltas only**. Cost: about 1 plan session + 1 short review. This keeps the gate honest and both fixes are mechanical.
2. **Accept Revision 1 with F1 + R4 as named Phase-1/Phase-2 obligations** (the exact wording in `f4b6b616`) and proceed to `breakdown`/implementation now. Cost: no extra planning; the risk is that the implementer applies the fixes without a plan-review check, and implementation review has to catch it.
3. **Stop here** and revisit the scope yourself (e.g. alongside LIN-3248's close-out work). Cost: LIN-2950 and its dependent LIN-2954 stay parked.

**If unanswered:** nothing proceeds on LIN-2950. No code has been written, so nothing is half-done. PROVISIONAL #1–#4 (peakRSS hidden; render-time scan fails closed; PR line carries its own `fetchedAt`; URL-shaped workspace keys stripped from ledger text) still await your look, independent of this choice.

Run summary: 4 steps stepped as 14 beats across 4 sessions (research `0ae5f096`, plan `b51e0ce1`, plan-review r1 `b29bd90a`, plan revision `3b53be9b`, plan-review r2 `5772bdf0`); every step's tracker write was re-fetched and verified.

issue.title: Improve the next-stage choice
issue.description:
Since LIN-3304, the next-stage choice has its own place. Now make it good.

In the first live trials (4 Oct; summary on LIN-3289), the work inside each stage was strong. Every slip was a judgement between stages:

* After a Request Changes review, the fix round got a fresh-start brief that didn't know about its PR or the review's findings.
* Engineering calls went to John as decisions: LIN-2950 was routed to him after plan review, and close-out filed LIN-3303. Harbour has one developer and one user. John decides product and intent; the agent decides engineering.
* The router never sees a ticket's relations (was LIN-3301).
* Two small defects turned up while isolating it: a `**Reasoning**` heading blanks the streamed recommendation (was LIN-3305), and `retro` is accepted as a route (was LIN-3306).

Measure first, from real cases (was LIN-3307), then improve against that measure. A wrong route is one that would harm the work: closing with findings still open, redoing finished work, or building without understanding. A wrong route matters; a suboptimal one is fine.

This is one coherent change. Keep it small, and finish it here rather than splitting it into follow-ups.

---

## Implementation Plan

Revision 3 — addresses plan-review findings.

One PR, fits one session.

comments.body:
## Research notes: LIN-3309, improve the next-stage choice (4 Oct, HEAD `98f766cc`)

**Staleness check.** Nothing has landed on `origin/main` since this ticket was created (14:08). `git log --since=2026-10-04T14:08:27Z` is empty, and HEAD is still the LIN-3304 merge, so every file:line below is at `98f766cc`.

**Sizing.** This is sized for one developer. LIN-3304's research was cut back for being about 10 times too big, so this recommends one PR with no programme around it. The measure is a handful of real cases plus unit tests.

---

### 1. The measure, from real cases

**Rule.** A route is wrong when it would harm the work: closing with findings still open, redoing finished work, building without understanding, or (from this ticket's own list) sending an engineering call to John. A suboptimal route counts as fine.

**How the cases were replayed.** Each real case was run through the live routing-only prompt (`buildRouterPrompt`, the writer-on path) on `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` at temperature 0, K=3–6 runs each. The spike script is in my scratchpad, not committed. Two cases were also replayed live through the proxy's `GET /issues/:id/recommend` on John's workspace settings.

| Case | State at the decision | Harmful routes | Right | HEAD result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **LIN-2950**, trail cut at 08:55:09 on 3 Oct, just after plan-review round 2 | 2nd Request Changes. Both findings are new (F1 drift from #1731, R4 a hole the revision opened); the reviewer says "neither needs a human preference" | `blocked` (engineering call to John); `breakdown`/`implementation` (building past open findings); `plan-review` (re-reviewing an unrevised plan) | `plan` | **blocked 5/6**, 5/5 and 3/3 across runs. Live proxy replay today: `blocked` |
| **LIN-2954**, live | Blocked by LIN-2950, 2949 and 2948, all In Progress | `research`/`plan`/`implementation` (work done now gets redone once the blockers land) | `blocked` | **research 2/3**. Live proxy replay: `research`, reasoning "Blockers: ✓ None" |
| **LIN-3304 fix round**, dispatch `dd572e67` | Review Request Changes; route was `implementation` (right) | The brief: it said "Branch… Open a PR" and nothing about the PR or the findings | brief tells the agent to continue the existing PR and answer each finding | Brief **identical to the first-pass one** apart from the Goal wording (diffed against `adb91024`). The agent recovered only because the ticket thread said "existing branch" |
| Guard `PR-1603-request-changes-1` | 1st Request Changes | anything but `plan` | `plan` | plan 6/6 |
| Guard `PR-1603-verdict-approve` | Approve | `plan-review`, `plan` | `implementation` | implementation 6/6 |
| Guard "third Request Changes" (the request-changes-2 bundle plus a 3rd verdict) | 3rd Request Changes, same finding | `plan`, `plan-review` (a loop) | `blocked` | blocked 4/6 |
| D1 (deterministic) | a `**Reasoning**` reply on the stream path | 0 live reasoning events | ≥1 | **0 events** (`StreamingSectionParser` waits for `## Reasoning\n`, openrouter.js:897); final parse still returns `plan` |
| D2 (deterministic) | `→ **retro**` | accepted | rejected | **accepted**: `routeStage` → `retro`, and `deriveDispatchKind('retro')` → `retro` |

**Does the measure track the real outcome? Yes, for these cases.** It reads red where the trials went wrong: both live replays reproduced the trial routes. It reads green on the guards. Two limits:

- **Noise.** Run-to-run noise on this model is about ±2 of 6 on the same prompt. The HEAD guard for request-changes-2 read 3/5, 3/5 and then 6/6 `blocked`. So small K proves little; use K=6 and look for shifts of 3 or more.
- **Which model.** My runs used the default router model, but John's workspace routes on its own setting. The two proxy replays did run on that setting and agree.
