comments.body:
## Research notes: LIN-3309, improve the next-stage choice (4 Oct, HEAD `98f766cc`)

**Staleness check.** Nothing has landed on `origin/main` since this ticket was created (14:08). `git log --since=2026-10-04T14:08:27Z` is empty, and HEAD is still the LIN-3304 merge, so every file:line below is at `98f766cc`.

**Sizing.** This is sized for one developer. LIN-3304's research was cut back for being about 10 times too big, so this recommends one PR with no programme around it. The measure is a handful of real cases plus unit tests.

---

### 1. The measure, from real cases

**Rule.** A route is wrong when it would harm the work: closing with findings still open, redoing finished work, building without understanding, or (from this ticket's own list) sending an engineering call to John. A suboptimal route counts as fine.

**How the cases were replayed.** Each real case was run through the live routing-only prompt (`buildRouterPrompt`, the writer-on path) on `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` at temperature 0, K=3–6 runs each. The spike script is in my scratchpad, not committed. Two cases were also replayed live through the proxy's `GET /issues/:id/recommend` on John's workspace settings.

| Case | State at the decision | Harmful routes | Right | HEAD result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **LIN-2950**, trail cut at 08:55:09 on 3 Oct, just after plan-review round 2 | 2nd Request Changes. Both findings are new (F1 drift from #1731, R4 a hole the revision opened); the reviewer says "neither needs a human preference" | `blocked` (engineering call to John); `breakdown`/`implementation` (building past open findings); `plan-review` (re-reviewing an unrevised plan) | `plan` | **blocked 5/6**, 5/5 and 3/3 across runs. Live proxy replay today: `blocked` |
| **LIN-2954**, live | Blocked by LIN-2950, 2949 and 2948, all In Progress | `research`/`plan`/`implementation` (work done now gets redone once the blockers land) | `blocked` | **research 2/3**. Live proxy replay: `research`, reasoning "Blockers: ✓ None" |
| **LIN-3304 fix round**, dispatch `dd572e67` | Review Request Changes; route was `implementation` (right) | The brief: it said "Branch… Open a PR" and nothing about the PR or the findings | brief tells the agent to continue the existing PR and answer each finding | Brief **identical to the first-pass one** apart from the Goal wording (diffed against `adb91024`). The agent recovered only because the ticket thread said "existing branch" |
| Guard `PR-1603-request-changes-1` | 1st Request Changes | anything but `plan` | `plan` | plan 6/6 |
| Guard `PR-1603-verdict-approve` | Approve | `plan-review`, `plan` | `implementation` | implementation 6/6 |
| Guard "third Request Changes" (the request-changes-2 bundle plus a 3rd verdict) | 3rd Request Changes, same finding | `plan`, `plan-review` (a loop) | `blocked` | blocked 4/6 |
| D1 (deterministic) | a `**Reasoning**` reply on the stream path | 0 live reasoning events | ≥1 | **0 events** (`StreamingSectionParser` waits for `## Reasoning\n`, openrouter.js:897); final parse still returns `plan` |
| D2 (deterministic) | `→ **retro**` | accepted | rejected | **accepted**: `routeStage` → `retro`, and `deriveDispatchKind('retro')` → `retro` |

**Does the measure track the real outcome? Yes, for these cases.** It reads red where the trials went wrong: both live replays reproduced the trial routes. It reads green on the guards. Two limits:

- **Noise.** Run-to-run noise on this model is about ±2 of 6 on the same prompt. The HEAD guard for request-changes-2 read 3/5, 3/5 and then 6/6 `blocked`. So small K proves little; use K=6 and look for shifts of 3 or more.
- **Which model.** My runs used the default router model, but John's workspace routes on its own setting. The two proxy replays did run on that setting and agree.

### 2. What causes each slip (verified)

**A. The router never sees relations (LIN-2954; also LIN-2950).**
- `ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY` selects relations only for children, grandchildren and parent.children, never for the issue itself (providers/linear/index.js:363-560).
- `formatIssueContext` renders none (openrouter.js:649-775).
- Router Step 2 tells the model to "detect this from the blocking relationship" (stage-router.js:166), so it guesses from prose.
- LIN-2950 shows the cost the other way round: its description says "Blocked until the sketches conversation is Done". LIN-2947 *is* Done, but the router can't see that, so it reasons "explicitly blocked" in most runs.

**B. The plan-review loop bound sends engineering findings to John (LIN-2950).**
- stage-router.js:199: "A SECOND Request Changes … → recommend `blocked`".
- The autopilot carries the same rule in its own prose (autopilot-kickoff.js:517; manual :61-64, :80-82), which is why it parked LIN-2950 at 08:56.
- What the record says about the bound:
  - It dates from LIN-1603 (`7f1efdb8`, 26 Jul).
  - `docs/papers/harbour/review-loops.md:21-30`: a send-back "asks for a member, not a design… None needed code to answer".
  - `why-legs-repeat.md:96-104`: a ruling preceded 21 of 30 third planning rounds (70%), and those rulings were go-aheads.
  - LIN-2950's own escalation recommended "authorise one narrow revision 2".
- So the bound mostly asks John an engineering question whose answer is "go on". This is the hand-off the ticket names.

**C. A fix-round brief has no revision branch (LIN-3304).**
- The plan template has "### Revising After a Plan Review" (prompt-template-defs.js:269-277): read the verdict, answer each finding, replace, don't append.
- The implementation template has no equivalent. Its Workflow says "Branch… Open a PR" unconditionally (prompt-template-defs.js:897-908).
- The router knew it was a fix round. But by design, nothing of the router's reasoning reaches the brief:
  - `routerFocus` passes only the → and Next lines (openrouter.js:1997);
  - the writer is told to "pass on none of its specifics" (prompts/brief-writer.js:70);
  - `briefFault` rejects copied router phrases (openrouter.js:2021).
- The cause is in the template, not the router. A template fix also reaches the paths where no router runs: autopilot pins, the UI stage buttons, and `?kind=`.

**D. LIN-3303 is not a routing slip.**
- Research on LIN-3140 raised `lin3140-b3-attach-freshness` with "file-followup" recommended, and close-out filed that follow-up while the ruling was still open.
- No next-stage choice was involved. The cause is in how a stage reads "a change the team would need to hear about" (prompts/brief-writer.js:7) when the team is one person. Those lines are served to every workspace, so hard-coding "one developer" there is a product question, not an engineering one.
- John already closed LIN-3303. I'm recording it, not proposing a change here and not filing anything.

**E. D1 and D2 (confirmed by running the code at HEAD).**
- **D1.**
  - The stream parser starts only on `## Reasoning\n` (openrouter.js:897).
  - Any other header form streams nothing, and so does a reply with no header at all, which `parseRouteDecision` accepts (stage-router.js:312-314). So the defect is wider than `**Reasoning**`.
  - The `done` event carries no reasoning.
- **D2.**
  - `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION = {'retro'}` (prompt-templates.js:427) only filters the vocabulary shown to the model.
  - No parse checks it. In routing mode, `composeRoutedRecommendation` → `writeStagePrompt('retro')` builds a real retro prompt (openrouter.js:2144-2149). In full mode, `retro` ships with the meta-written body.

### 3. Spike: do the fixes move the routes?

Same harness, K=6 unless noted.

| Variant | LIN-2954 | LIN-2950 (decision point) | 3rd-RC guard | RC-1 / Approve guards |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HEAD | research 2/3 | blocked 5/6 | blocked 4/6 | plan 6/6 / implement 6/6 |
| Relations rendered as one "Blocked by: … (Done)" list | — | blocked 4/5 (the model reads "(Done)" items as still blocking) | — | — |
| Relations split as `Blocked by (open):` and `Blockers already resolved:` | **blocked 3/3** | blocked 3/6 alone | — | — |
| + bound in prose: "new findings → plan, a repeated finding → blocked" (several wordings) | — | plan 6/6 on the best wording | **regressed**: the repeated-finding guard went plan 5/5. The model can't tell "same finding" from prose | held |
| + bound by count (1st/2nd RC → plan, 3rd → blocked), prose only | — | plan 4/6 | blocked 3/6, plan-review 3/6 (miscounts) | held |
| **+ bound by count, with the count done in code** (a `PLAN-REVIEW FACTS` line, like FRONTIER FACTS) | — | **plan 4/6 and 3/6**; residual `blocked` cites the trail's own echo of the old rule ("a second Request Changes goes to the human"); 1 breakdown | **blocked 6/6** | plan 6/6 / implement 6/6 |

**What the spike shows:**
- **Facts computed in code work; prose rules are noisy in both directions.** This matches `where-judgement-happens.md:201` ("put the rule-class calls in code: escalate at the loop bound…") and the FRONTIER FACTS precedent (stage-router.js:96-104).
- **The verdict counter is cheap and needs no new parser.**
  - The contract already requires plan-review comments to start `### Plan Review Verdict` (prompt-contract.js:28).
  - `extractVerdict` exists (plan-review-round-trips.js:268).
  - Legacy trails like LIN-2950 (`## Plan-review (round 2) — Request Changes`) need a first-line fallback, because `extractVerdict` returns null on them.
  - Autopilot step records start with `**Autopilot`, so a heading test excludes them.
- **"Never route past an unanswered verdict to breakdown or implementation" must stay in the wording.** Dropping it brought back `breakdown` picks.

---

### Per-layer audit

**L1. Router prompt fragments (lib/stage-router.js:77-265)**
- Shared byte-for-byte by the writer-off full template (meta-prompt-template.js:89) and the writer-on `buildRouterPrompt` (:294).
- The bound text is at :196-199.
- A change must keep the shared-fragment property and regenerate the 8 byte snapshots in `tests/fixtures/stage-router-prompts/` (regenerator `scripts/eval/regen-stage-router-snapshots.mjs`) and `scripts/eval/meta-prompt.baseline.txt`. That is an intended diff, reviewed as text.

**L2. Router inputs (formatIssueContext, openrouter.js:649; assembleMetaPromptArgs :786)**
- There is no relation data at issue level today.
- Computed facts enter the prompt as a "deterministic, do not re-derive" block (frontierFactsBlock, stage-router.js:96). A plan-review fact block should follow that pattern, computed beside `assembleNodeFacts` (recommendation-facts.js:89).

**L3. Providers (fetchRecommendationContext)**
- **Linear** (index.js:1157 → fetchIssueContext :821): add issue-level `inverseRelations { nodes { type issue { identifier title state { name type } } } }` and normalise it to `issue.blockedBy`. The children's selection already fetches the same shape (:455-466).
- **Local** has relations (`_relationConnections`, local/index.js:527-551) but doesn't put them in fetchIssueContext (:235-290). Add them there.
- **GitHub, GitHub Projects and Jira** have no typed relations (github/index.js:53, :265; jira :512). Nothing to do, and the render is gated on presence.

**L4. formatIssueContext consumers.** openrouter.js:788 (router and meta), brief.js:57, recap.js:37, scan.js:84, task-chat-template.js:39, plus eval scripts.
- All of them gain the line only when the issue has blockers.
- Caches hash named fields only (recap-cache.js:44-70, scan-fingerprint.js:138-160), so nothing churns.

**L5. Parse and stream (stage-router.js:310-339; openrouter.js:874-955, 970-1215, 1769)**
- D2 belongs in the seam: one check that rejects a kind in `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION`, used by `parseRouteDecision` and by full-mode `parseRecommendationResponse`.
- Full mode's unknown-name → `custom` behaviour stays as it is. That is a separate behaviour, and the ticket only asks about `retro`.
- **D1 fix:** after the final parse, if the stream emitted no reasoning, emit one reasoning delta with `parsed.reasoning`. This is the same catch-up pattern the prompt section already uses (openrouter.js:1186-1192). The header grammar then has one owner (the seam), and no second regex is added.

**L6. Implementation template (prompt-template-defs.js:883-944)**
- The process is code-owned on every path (LIN-3299), so text added here reaches routed, pinned and fixed dispatches alike.
- Mirror the plan template's revision section (:269-277), and make Workflow steps 3 and 7 conditional, so the brief no longer says "Open a PR" in a fix round.

**L7. Parallel deciders: the autopilot's own copy of the bound.** autopilot-kickoff.js:517 and docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md:61-64, :80-82. These must move with L1, or the autopilot keeps parking at the second round on its own reading.

**L8. The planner's own bound (prompt-template-defs.js:277)**
- It currently reads "a plan that comes back a second time still carrying the same findings escalates to a human".
- It is the in-stage home for "same finding" judgement, and Opus reads the findings in full. Reword it to agree with the count: a third verdict escalates, and a repeated finding is answered or fixed in this pass.

**L9. Size freeze (tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js)**
- Every frozen ceiling sits exactly at its file size: stage-router.js 45728 B, prompt-template-defs.js 127237 B, prompt-templates.js 20707 B. `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES` is 575524.
- Text added must be paid by text removed in the same change. Named candidates:
  - the now-stale "behaviour deliberately unchanged / defects fixed later" paragraphs (stage-router.js:12-15, :301-303);
  - the history clause in implementation guideline 6 (prompt-template-defs.js, "This extends the acceptance-witness discipline…");
  - the bound bullets themselves, which can be rewritten shorter.
- The autopilot kickoff and manual are not frozen.

**L10. Tests and evals that pin current behaviour**
- Bound text: openrouter.test.js:986-990, :3405.
- Present-behaviour pins for D1 and D2: stage-router.test.js, per the LIN-3304 close-out. These flip from "present" to "fixed".
- `plan-review-gate.json`: request-changes-2 expects `blocked` today. It becomes `plan`, plus a new 3rd-RC case expecting `blocked`.

### Closing the set
**Searches run:**
- The bound: `SECOND Request Changes|revision cycle|second time still carrying|third pass` over lib, routes, docs, scripts and tests.
- `formatIssueContext(`.
- `fetchRecommendationContext`.
- `new StreamingSectionParser`: one site, openrouter.js:1064.
- `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION`.
- `kind:decision`.
- Every dispatched prompt for the LIN-3304, LIN-3140 and LIN-2950 trials, read through the proxy.

**Checked and left alone:**
- **docs/papers/\*\*:** historical record.
- **scripts/survey-hides-prompts.mjs:70:** a paper script whose anchor already went stale when LIN-3304 moved the text.
- **plan-review-round-trips.js:26:** a historical comment.
- **The brief writer's `copied-router` guard:** cause C is fixed without passing router text, so John's open ruling on "may a brief name what the router found" is not needed.

**The set would be wrong if:**
- another served prompt restates the plan-review bound in words my grep missed (e.g. "loop limit"). The passage runner and worker lane prompts came back empty for these terms.
- a non-Linear provider exposes relations under another field.

### Options considered
| Option | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Fix at the four causes, in code where the rule is mechanical** (recommended) | The spike shows each one moves its case. Facts in code beat prose. Fixes on the brief reach pinned paths too | Touches frozen surfaces, so bytes must be paid. The bound change revises a rule John set (LIN-1603), but this ticket names its effect as a slip |
| 2. Prose-only rewording of the bound ("new findings → plan, a repeated finding → blocked") | No new code | The spike regressed the repeated-finding guard (plan 5/5); the model can't judge "same finding" |
| 3. Pass the router's Next line into the brief for fix rounds | Reuses what the router knows | It needs John's open ruling, it misses pinned paths, and it reverses the `copied-router` guard |
| 4. Retry or vote at temperature 0 to cut noise | Smooths variance | Cost, and it treats the symptom; facts remove the guess |

### Surface Assessment
**Surface Assessment: [lands cleanly]**

Each change extends a model that already exists, and none adds a second representation:
- **Relations.** The provider already fetches this exact shape for children (index.js:455-466). This only selects it at issue level and renders it.
- **The verdict count.** It reuses `extractVerdict` and the contract heading, and joins the existing deterministic-facts block pattern.
- **The fix round.** It mirrors the plan template's existing revision section.
- **D1** reuses the existing catch-up delta, and **D2** reuses the existing exclusion set.

The size freeze is a constraint the plan must budget for, not a refactor.

**Who pays:**
- formatIssueContext's other consumers (brief, recap, scan, task chat) pay a line of tokens on blocked issues only, and gain accurate state.
- Linear `fetchIssueContext` callers pay one more small nested selection.
- The writer-off full path gets the same fragment changes. That is intended, since the paths share fragments.

**Note on the research (FC, after reading it):** it's the right size and holds up against the code. Three things to carry into the next stage:

1. **The plan-review count needs to reset after John rules or the plan is revised.** As written, a count of 3 stays at 3, so every later route is `blocked` and goes back to John.
2. **Measure with the existing routing harness** (`scripts/eval/jev-routing-eval.mjs`, LIN-3107: 66 fixtures, 79.1% at K=5). Add today's cases to it and compare before and after across all of them, instead of a separate script.
3. **State the pass bar before changing anything.** LIN-2950 reached only 3 to 4 of 6 in the spike.

On the fix round: if code already knows there's an open PR with a Request Changes review, let code switch the template's revision steps on, rather than a sentence that asks the agent to work it out.

The cited grep (`SECOND Request Changes|revision cycle|second time still carrying|third pass`) finds the wording of the bullet, not the rule. A grep for the concept finds more.

issue.title: Improve the next-stage choice
issue.description:
Since LIN-3304, the next-stage choice has its own place. Now make it good.

In the first live trials (4 Oct; summary on LIN-3289), the work inside each stage was strong. Every slip was a judgement between stages:

* After a Request Changes review, the fix round got a fresh-start brief that didn't know about its PR or the review's findings.
* Engineering calls went to John as decisions: LIN-2950 was routed to him after plan review, and close-out filed LIN-3303. Harbour has one developer and one user. John decides product and intent; the agent decides engineering.
* The router never sees a ticket's relations (was LIN-3301).
* Two small defects turned up while isolating it: a `**Reasoning**` heading blanks the streamed recommendation (was LIN-3305), and `retro` is accepted as a route (was LIN-3306).

Measure first, from real cases (was LIN-3307), then improve against that measure. A wrong route is one that would harm the work: closing with findings still open, redoing finished work, or building without understanding. A wrong route matters; a suboptimal one is fine.

This is one coherent change. Keep it small, and finish it here rather than splitting it into follow-ups.

---

## Implementation Plan

Revision 3 — addresses plan-review findings.

One PR, fits one session.

comments.body:
## Research notes: LIN-3309, improve the next-stage choice (4 Oct, HEAD `98f766cc`)

**Staleness check.** Nothing has landed on `origin/main` since this ticket was created (14:08). `git log --since=2026-10-04T14:08:27Z` is empty, and HEAD is still the LIN-3304 merge, so every file:line below is at `98f766cc`.

**Sizing.** This is sized for one developer. LIN-3304's research was cut back for being about 10 times too big, so this recommends one PR with no programme around it. The measure is a handful of real cases plus unit tests.

---

### 1. The measure, from real cases

**Rule.** A route is wrong when it would harm the work: closing with findings still open, redoing finished work, building without understanding, or (from this ticket's own list) sending an engineering call to John. A suboptimal route counts as fine.

**How the cases were replayed.** Each real case was run through the live routing-only prompt (`buildRouterPrompt`, the writer-on path) on `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` at temperature 0, K=3–6 runs each. The spike script is in my scratchpad, not committed. Two cases were also replayed live through the proxy's `GET /issues/:id/recommend` on John's workspace settings.

| Case | State at the decision | Harmful routes | Right | HEAD result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **LIN-2950**, trail cut at 08:55:09 on 3 Oct, just after plan-review round 2 | 2nd Request Changes. Both findings are new (F1 drift from #1731, R4 a hole the revision opened); the reviewer says "neither needs a human preference" | `blocked` (engineering call to John); `breakdown`/`implementation` (building past open findings); `plan-review` (re-reviewing an unrevised plan) | `plan` | **blocked 5/6**, 5/5 and 3/3 across runs. Live proxy replay today: `blocked` |
| **LIN-2954**, live | Blocked by LIN-2950, 2949 and 2948, all In Progress | `research`/`plan`/`implementation` (work done now gets redone once the blockers land) | `blocked` | **research 2/3**. Live proxy replay: `research`, reasoning "Blockers: ✓ None" |
| **LIN-3304 fix round**, dispatch `dd572e67` | Review Request Changes; route was `implementation` (right) | The brief: it said "Branch… Open a PR" and nothing about the PR or the findings | brief tells the agent to continue the existing PR and answer each finding | Brief **identical to the first-pass one** apart from the Goal wording (diffed against `adb91024`). The agent recovered only because the ticket thread said "existing branch" |
| Guard `PR-1603-request-changes-1` | 1st Request Changes | anything but `plan` | `plan` | plan 6/6 |
| Guard `PR-1603-verdict-approve` | Approve | `plan-review`, `plan` | `implementation` | implementation 6/6 |
| Guard "third Request Changes" (the request-changes-2 bundle plus a 3rd verdict) | 3rd Request Changes, same finding | `plan`, `plan-review` (a loop) | `blocked` | blocked 4/6 |
| D1 (deterministic) | a `**Reasoning**` reply on the stream path | 0 live reasoning events | ≥1 | **0 events** (`StreamingSectionParser` waits for `## Reasoning\n`, openrouter.js:897); final parse still returns `plan` |
| D2 (deterministic) | `→ **retro**` | accepted | rejected | **accepted**: `routeStage` → `retro`, and `deriveDispatchKind('retro')` → `retro` |

**Does the measure track the real outcome? Yes, for these cases.** It reads red where the trials went wrong: both live replays reproduced the trial routes. It reads green on the guards. Two limits:

- **Noise.** Run-to-run noise on this model is about ±2 of 6 on the same prompt. The HEAD guard for request-changes-2 read 3/5, 3/5 and then 6/6 `blocked`. So small K proves little; use K=6 and look for shifts of 3 or more.
- **Which model.** My runs used the default router model, but John's workspace routes on its own setting. The two proxy replays did run on that setting and agree.

### 2. What causes each slip (verified)

**A. The router never sees relations (LIN-2954; also LIN-2950).**
- `ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY` selects relations only for children, grandchildren and parent.children, never for the issue itself (providers/linear/index.js:363-560).
- `formatIssueContext` renders none (openrouter.js:649-775).
- Router Step 2 tells the model to "detect this from the blocking relationship" (stage-router.js:166), so it guesses from prose.
- LIN-2950 shows the cost the other way round: its description says "Blocked until the sketches conversation is Done". LIN-2947 *is* Done, but the router can't see that, so it reasons "explicitly blocked" in most runs.

**B. The plan-review loop bound sends engineering findings to John (LIN-2950).**
- stage-router.js:199: "A SECOND Request Changes … → recommend `blocked`".
- The autopilot carries the same rule in its own prose (autopilot-kickoff.js:517; manual :61-64, :80-82), which is why it parked LIN-2950 at 08:56.
- What the record says about the bound:
  - It dates from LIN-1603 (`7f1efdb8`, 26 Jul).
  - `docs/papers/harbour/review-loops.md:21-30`: a send-back "asks for a member, not a design… None needed code to answer".
  - `why-legs-repeat.md:96-104`: a ruling preceded 21 of 30 third planning rounds (70%), and those rulings were go-aheads.
  - LIN-2950's own escalation recommended "authorise one narrow revision 2".
- So the bound mostly asks John an engineering question whose answer is "go on". This is the hand-off the ticket names.

**C. A fix-round brief has no revision branch (LIN-3304).**
- The plan template has "### Revising After a Plan Review" (prompt-template-defs.js:269-277): read the verdict, answer each finding, replace, don't append.
- The implementation template has no equivalent. Its Workflow says "Branch… Open a PR" unconditionally (prompt-template-defs.js:897-908).
- The router knew it was a fix round. But by design, nothing of the router's reasoning reaches the brief:
  - `routerFocus` passes only the → and Next lines (openrouter.js:1997);
  - the writer is told to "pass on none of its specifics" (prompts/brief-writer.js:70);
  - `briefFault` rejects copied router phrases (openrouter.js:2021).
- The cause is in the template, not the router. A template fix also reaches the paths where no router runs: autopilot pins, the UI stage buttons, and `?kind=`.

**D. LIN-3303 is not a routing slip.**
- Research on LIN-3140 raised `lin3140-b3-attach-freshness` with "file-followup" recommended, and close-out filed that follow-up while the ruling was still open.
- No next-stage choice was involved. The cause is in how a stage reads "a change the team would need to hear about" (prompts/brief-writer.js:7) when the team is one person. Those lines are served to every workspace, so hard-coding "one developer" there is a product question, not an engineering one.
- John already closed LIN-3303. I'm recording it, not proposing a change here and not filing anything.

**E. D1 and D2 (confirmed by running the code at HEAD).**
- **D1.**
  - The stream parser starts only on `## Reasoning\n` (openrouter.js:897).
  - Any other header form streams nothing, and so does a reply with no header at all, which `parseRouteDecision` accepts (stage-router.js:312-314). So the defect is wider than `**Reasoning**`.
  - The `done` event carries no reasoning.
- **D2.**
  - `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION = {'retro'}` (prompt-templates.js:427) only filters the vocabulary shown to the model.
  - No parse checks it. In routing mode, `composeRoutedRecommendation` → `writeStagePrompt('retro')` builds a real retro prompt (openrouter.js:2144-2149). In full mode, `retro` ships with the meta-written body.

### 3. Spike: do the fixes move the routes?

Same harness, K=6 unless noted.

| Variant | LIN-2954 | LIN-2950 (decision point) | 3rd-RC guard | RC-1 / Approve guards |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HEAD | research 2/3 | blocked 5/6 | blocked 4/6 | plan 6/6 / implement 6/6 |
| Relations rendered as one "Blocked by: … (Done)" list | — | blocked 4/5 (the model reads "(Done)" items as still blocking) | — | — |
| Relations split as `Blocked by (open):` and `Blockers already resolved:` | **blocked 3/3** | blocked 3/6 alone | — | — |
| + bound in prose: "new findings → plan, a repeated finding → blocked" (several wordings) | — | plan 6/6 on the best wording | **regressed**: the repeated-finding guard went plan 5/5. The model can't tell "same finding" from prose | held |
| + bound by count (1st/2nd RC → plan, 3rd → blocked), prose only | — | plan 4/6 | blocked 3/6, plan-review 3/6 (miscounts) | held |
| **+ bound by count, with the count done in code** (a `PLAN-REVIEW FACTS` line, like FRONTIER FACTS) | — | **plan 4/6 and 3/6**; residual `blocked` cites the trail's own echo of the old rule ("a second Request Changes goes to the human"); 1 breakdown | **blocked 6/6** | plan 6/6 / implement 6/6 |

**What the spike shows:**
- **Facts computed in code work; prose rules are noisy in both directions.** This matches `where-judgement-happens.md:201` ("put the rule-class calls in code: escalate at the loop bound…") and the FRONTIER FACTS precedent (stage-router.js:96-104).
- **The verdict counter is cheap and needs no new parser.**
  - The contract already requires plan-review comments to start `### Plan Review Verdict` (prompt-contract.js:28).
  - `extractVerdict` exists (plan-review-round-trips.js:268).
  - Legacy trails like LIN-2950 (`## Plan-review (round 2) — Request Changes`) need a first-line fallback, because `extractVerdict` returns null on them.
  - Autopilot step records start with `**Autopilot`, so a heading test excludes them.
- **"Never route past an unanswered verdict to breakdown or implementation" must stay in the wording.** Dropping it brought back `breakdown` picks.

---

### Per-layer audit

**L1. Router prompt fragments (lib/stage-router.js:77-265)**
- Shared byte-for-byte by the writer-off full template (meta-prompt-template.js:89) and the writer-on `buildRouterPrompt` (:294).
- The bound text is at :196-199.
- A change must keep the shared-fragment property and regenerate the 8 byte snapshots in `tests/fixtures/stage-router-prompts/` (regenerator `scripts/eval/regen-stage-router-snapshots.mjs`) and `scripts/eval/meta-prompt.baseline.txt`. That is an intended diff, reviewed as text.

**L2. Router inputs (formatIssueContext, openrouter.js:649; assembleMetaPromptArgs :786)**
- There is no relation data at issue level today.
- Computed facts enter the prompt as a "deterministic, do not re-derive" block (frontierFactsBlock, stage-router.js:96). A plan-review fact block should follow that pattern, computed beside `assembleNodeFacts` (recommendation-facts.js:89).

**L3. Providers (fetchRecommendationContext)**
- **Linear** (index.js:1157 → fetchIssueContext :821): add issue-level `inverseRelations { nodes { type issue { identifier title state { name type } } } }` and normalise it to `issue.blockedBy`. The children's selection already fetches the same shape (:455-466).
- **Local** has relations (`_relationConnections`, local/index.js:527-551) but doesn't put them in fetchIssueContext (:235-290). Add them there.
- **GitHub, GitHub Projects and Jira** have no typed relations (github/index.js:53, :265; jira :512). Nothing to do, and the render is gated on presence.

**L4. formatIssueContext consumers.** openrouter.js:788 (router and meta), brief.js:57, recap.js:37, scan.js:84, task-chat-template.js:39, plus eval scripts.
- All of them gain the line only when the issue has blockers.
- Caches hash named fields only (recap-cache.js:44-70, scan-fingerprint.js:138-160), so nothing churns.

**L5. Parse and stream (stage-router.js:310-339; openrouter.js:874-955, 970-1215, 1769)**
- D2 belongs in the seam: one check that rejects a kind in `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION`, used by `parseRouteDecision` and by full-mode `parseRecommendationResponse`.
- Full mode's unknown-name → `custom` behaviour stays as it is. That is a separate behaviour, and the ticket only asks about `retro`.
- **D1 fix:** after the final parse, if the stream emitted no reasoning, emit one reasoning delta with `parsed.reasoning`. This is the same catch-up pattern the prompt section already uses (openrouter.js:1186-1192). The header grammar then has one owner (the seam), and no second regex is added.

**L6. Implementation template (prompt-template-defs.js:883-944)**
- The process is code-owned on every path (LIN-3299), so text added here reaches routed, pinned and fixed dispatches alike.
- Mirror the plan template's revision section (:269-277), and make Workflow steps 3 and 7 conditional, so the brief no longer says "Open a PR" in a fix round.

**L7. Parallel deciders: the autopilot's own copy of the bound.** autopilot-kickoff.js:517 and docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md:61-64, :80-82. These must move with L1, or the autopilot keeps parking at the second round on its own reading.

**L8. The planner's own bound (prompt-template-defs.js:277)**
- It currently reads "a plan that comes back a second time still carrying the same findings escalates to a human".
- It is the in-stage home for "same finding" judgement, and Opus reads the findings in full. Reword it to agree with the count: a third verdict escalates, and a repeated finding is answered or fixed in this pass.

**L9. Size freeze (tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js)**
- Every frozen ceiling sits exactly at its file size: stage-router.js 45728 B, prompt-template-defs.js 127237 B, prompt-templates.js 20707 B. `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES` is 575524.
- Text added must be paid by text removed in the same change. Named candidates:
  - the now-stale "behaviour deliberately unchanged / defects fixed later" paragraphs (stage-router.js:12-15, :301-303);
  - the history clause in implementation guideline 6 (prompt-template-defs.js, "This extends the acceptance-witness discipline…");
  - the bound bullets themselves, which can be rewritten shorter.
- The autopilot kickoff and manual are not frozen.

**L10. Tests and evals that pin current behaviour**
- Bound text: openrouter.test.js:986-990, :3405.
- Present-behaviour pins for D1 and D2: stage-router.test.js, per the LIN-3304 close-out. These flip from "present" to "fixed".
- `plan-review-gate.json`: request-changes-2 expects `blocked` today. It becomes `plan`, plus a new 3rd-RC case expecting `blocked`.

### Closing the set
**Searches run:**
- The bound: `SECOND Request Changes|revision cycle|second time still carrying|third pass` over lib, routes, docs, scripts and tests.
- `formatIssueContext(`.
- `fetchRecommendationContext`.
- `new StreamingSectionParser`: one site, openrouter.js:1064.
- `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION`.
- `kind:decision`.
- Every dispatched prompt for the LIN-3304, LIN-3140 and LIN-2950 trials, read through the proxy.

**Checked and left alone:**
- **docs/papers/\*\*:** historical record.
- **scripts/survey-hides-prompts.mjs:70:** a paper script whose anchor already went stale when LIN-3304 moved the text.
- **plan-review-round-trips.js:26:** a historical comment.
- **The brief writer's `copied-router` guard:** cause C is fixed without passing router text, so John's open ruling on "may a brief name what the router found" is not needed.

**The set would be wrong if:**
- another served prompt restates the plan-review bound in words my grep missed (e.g. "loop limit"). The passage runner and worker lane prompts came back empty for these terms.
- a non-Linear provider exposes relations under another field.

### Options considered
| Option | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Fix at the four causes, in code where the rule is mechanical** (recommended) | The spike shows each one moves its case. Facts in code beat prose. Fixes on the brief reach pinned paths too | Touches frozen surfaces, so bytes must be paid. The bound change revises a rule John set (LIN-1603), but this ticket names its effect as a slip |
| 2. Prose-only rewording of the bound ("new findings → plan, a repeated finding → blocked") | No new code | The spike regressed the repeated-finding guard (plan 5/5); the model can't judge "same finding" |
| 3. Pass the router's Next line into the brief for fix rounds | Reuses what the router knows | It needs John's open ruling, it misses pinned paths, and it reverses the `copied-router` guard |
| 4. Retry or vote at temperature 0 to cut noise | Smooths variance | Cost, and it treats the symptom; facts remove the guess |

### Surface Assessment
**Surface Assessment: [lands cleanly]**

Each change extends a model that already exists, and none adds a second representation:
- **Relations.** The provider already fetches this exact shape for children (index.js:455-466). This only selects it at issue level and renders it.
- **The verdict count.** It reuses `extractVerdict` and the contract heading, and joins the existing deterministic-facts block pattern.
- **The fix round.** It mirrors the plan template's existing revision section.
- **D1** reuses the existing catch-up delta, and **D2** reuses the existing exclusion set.

The size freeze is a constraint the plan must budget for, not a refactor.

**Who pays:**
- formatIssueContext's other consumers (brief, recap, scan, task chat) pay a line of tokens on blocked issues only, and gain accurate state.
- Linear `fetchIssueContext` callers pay one more small nested selection.
- The writer-off full path gets the same fragment changes. That is intended, since the paths share fragments.

**Note on the research (FC, after reading it):** it's the right size and holds up against the code. Three things to carry into the next stage:

1. **The plan-review count needs to reset after John rules or the plan is revised.** As written, a count of 3 stays at 3, so every later route is `blocked` and goes back to John.
2. **Measure with the existing routing harness** (`scripts/eval/jev-routing-eval.mjs`, LIN-3107: 66 fixtures, 79.1% at K=5). Add today's cases to it and compare before and after across all of them, instead of a separate script.

On the fix round: if code already knows there's an open PR with a Request Changes review, let code switch the template's revision steps on, rather than a sentence that asks the agent to work it out.

issue.title: Improve the next-stage choice
issue.description:
Since LIN-3304, the next-stage choice has its own place. Now make it good.

In the first live trials (4 Oct; summary on LIN-3289), the work inside each stage was strong. Every slip was a judgement between stages:

* After a Request Changes review, the fix round got a fresh-start brief that didn't know about its PR or the review's findings.
* Engineering calls went to John as decisions: LIN-2950 was routed to him after plan review, and close-out filed LIN-3303. Harbour has one developer and one user. John decides product and intent; the agent decides engineering.
* The router never sees a ticket's relations (was LIN-3301).
* Two small defects turned up while isolating it: a `**Reasoning**` heading blanks the streamed recommendation (was LIN-3305), and `retro` is accepted as a route (was LIN-3306).

Measure first, from real cases (was LIN-3307), then improve against that measure. A wrong route is one that would harm the work: closing with findings still open, redoing finished work, or building without understanding. A wrong route matters; a suboptimal one is fine.

This is one coherent change. Keep it small, and finish it here rather than splitting it into follow-ups.

---

## Implementation Plan

Revision 3 — addresses plan-review findings.

One PR, fits one session.

comments.body:
## Research notes: LIN-3309, improve the next-stage choice (4 Oct, HEAD `98f766cc`)

**Staleness check.** Nothing has landed on `origin/main` since this ticket was created (14:08). `git log --since=2026-10-04T14:08:27Z` is empty, and HEAD is still the LIN-3304 merge, so every file:line below is at `98f766cc`.

**Sizing.** This is sized for one developer. LIN-3304's research was cut back for being about 10 times too big, so this recommends one PR with no programme around it. The measure is a handful of real cases plus unit tests.

---

### 1. The measure, from real cases

**Rule.** A route is wrong when it would harm the work: closing with findings still open, redoing finished work, building without understanding, or (from this ticket's own list) sending an engineering call to John. A suboptimal route counts as fine.

**How the cases were replayed.** Each real case was run through the live routing-only prompt (`buildRouterPrompt`, the writer-on path) on `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` at temperature 0, K=3–6 runs each. The spike script is in my scratchpad, not committed. Two cases were also replayed live through the proxy's `GET /issues/:id/recommend` on John's workspace settings.

| Case | State at the decision | Harmful routes | Right | HEAD result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **LIN-2950**, trail cut at 08:55:09 on 3 Oct, just after plan-review round 2 | 2nd Request Changes. Both findings are new (F1 drift from #1731, R4 a hole the revision opened); the reviewer says "neither needs a human preference" | `blocked` (engineering call to John); `breakdown`/`implementation` (building past open findings); `plan-review` (re-reviewing an unrevised plan) | `plan` | **blocked 5/6**, 5/5 and 3/3 across runs. Live proxy replay today: `blocked` |
| **LIN-2954**, live | Blocked by LIN-2950, 2949 and 2948, all In Progress | `research`/`plan`/`implementation` (work done now gets redone once the blockers land) | `blocked` | **research 2/3**. Live proxy replay: `research`, reasoning "Blockers: ✓ None" |
| **LIN-3304 fix round**, dispatch `dd572e67` | Review Request Changes; route was `implementation` (right) | The brief: it said "Branch… Open a PR" and nothing about the PR or the findings | brief tells the agent to continue the existing PR and answer each finding | Brief **identical to the first-pass one** apart from the Goal wording (diffed against `adb91024`). The agent recovered only because the ticket thread said "existing branch" |
| Guard `PR-1603-request-changes-1` | 1st Request Changes | anything but `plan` | `plan` | plan 6/6 |
| Guard `PR-1603-verdict-approve` | Approve | `plan-review`, `plan` | `implementation` | implementation 6/6 |
| Guard "third Request Changes" (the request-changes-2 bundle plus a 3rd verdict) | 3rd Request Changes, same finding | `plan`, `plan-review` (a loop) | `blocked` | blocked 4/6 |
| D1 (deterministic) | a `**Reasoning**` reply on the stream path | 0 live reasoning events | ≥1 | **0 events** (`StreamingSectionParser` waits for `## Reasoning\n`, openrouter.js:897); final parse still returns `plan` |
| D2 (deterministic) | `→ **retro**` | accepted | rejected | **accepted**: `routeStage` → `retro`, and `deriveDispatchKind('retro')` → `retro` |

**Does the measure track the real outcome? Yes, for these cases.** It reads red where the trials went wrong: both live replays reproduced the trial routes. It reads green on the guards. Two limits:

- **Noise.** Run-to-run noise on this model is about ±2 of 6 on the same prompt. The HEAD guard for request-changes-2 read 3/5, 3/5 and then 6/6 `blocked`. So small K proves little; use K=6 and look for shifts of 3 or more.
- **Which model.** My runs used the default router model, but John's workspace routes on its own setting. The two proxy replays did run on that setting and agree.

### 2. What causes each slip (verified)

**A. The router never sees relations (LIN-2954; also LIN-2950).**
- `ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY` selects relations only for children, grandchildren and parent.children, never for the issue itself (providers/linear/index.js:363-560).
- `formatIssueContext` renders none (openrouter.js:649-775).
- Router Step 2 tells the model to "detect this from the blocking relationship" (stage-router.js:166), so it guesses from prose.
- LIN-2950 shows the cost the other way round: its description says "Blocked until the sketches conversation is Done". LIN-2947 *is* Done, but the router can't see that, so it reasons "explicitly blocked" in most runs.

**B. The plan-review loop bound sends engineering findings to John (LIN-2950).**
- stage-router.js:199: "A SECOND Request Changes … → recommend `blocked`".
- The autopilot carries the same rule in its own prose (autopilot-kickoff.js:517; manual :61-64, :80-82), which is why it parked LIN-2950 at 08:56.
- What the record says about the bound:
  - It dates from LIN-1603 (`7f1efdb8`, 26 Jul).
  - `docs/papers/harbour/review-loops.md:21-30`: a send-back "asks for a member, not a design… None needed code to answer".
  - `why-legs-repeat.md:96-104`: a ruling preceded 21 of 30 third planning rounds (70%), and those rulings were go-aheads.
  - LIN-2950's own escalation recommended "authorise one narrow revision 2".
- So the bound mostly asks John an engineering question whose answer is "go on". This is the hand-off the ticket names.

**C. A fix-round brief has no revision branch (LIN-3304).**
- The plan template has "### Revising After a Plan Review" (prompt-template-defs.js:269-277): read the verdict, answer each finding, replace, don't append.
- The implementation template has no equivalent. Its Workflow says "Branch… Open a PR" unconditionally (prompt-template-defs.js:897-908).
- The router knew it was a fix round. But by design, nothing of the router's reasoning reaches the brief:
  - `routerFocus` passes only the → and Next lines (openrouter.js:1997);
  - the writer is told to "pass on none of its specifics" (prompts/brief-writer.js:70);
  - `briefFault` rejects copied router phrases (openrouter.js:2021).
- The cause is in the template, not the router. A template fix also reaches the paths where no router runs: autopilot pins, the UI stage buttons, and `?kind=`.

**D. LIN-3303 is not a routing slip.**
- Research on LIN-3140 raised `lin3140-b3-attach-freshness` with "file-followup" recommended, and close-out filed that follow-up while the ruling was still open.
- No next-stage choice was involved. The cause is in how a stage reads "a change the team would need to hear about" (prompts/brief-writer.js:7) when the team is one person. Those lines are served to every workspace, so hard-coding "one developer" there is a product question, not an engineering one.
- John already closed LIN-3303. I'm recording it, not proposing a change here and not filing anything.

**E. D1 and D2 (confirmed by running the code at HEAD).**
- **D1.**
  - The stream parser starts only on `## Reasoning\n` (openrouter.js:897).
  - Any other header form streams nothing, and so does a reply with no header at all, which `parseRouteDecision` accepts (stage-router.js:312-314). So the defect is wider than `**Reasoning**`.
  - The `done` event carries no reasoning.
- **D2.**
  - `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION = {'retro'}` (prompt-templates.js:427) only filters the vocabulary shown to the model.
  - No parse checks it. In routing mode, `composeRoutedRecommendation` → `writeStagePrompt('retro')` builds a real retro prompt (openrouter.js:2144-2149). In full mode, `retro` ships with the meta-written body.

### 3. Spike: do the fixes move the routes?

Same harness, K=6 unless noted.

| Variant | LIN-2954 | LIN-2950 (decision point) | 3rd-RC guard | RC-1 / Approve guards |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HEAD | research 2/3 | blocked 5/6 | blocked 4/6 | plan 6/6 / implement 6/6 |
| Relations rendered as one "Blocked by: … (Done)" list | — | blocked 4/5 (the model reads "(Done)" items as still blocking) | — | — |
| Relations split as `Blocked by (open):` and `Blockers already resolved:` | **blocked 3/3** | blocked 3/6 alone | — | — |
| + bound in prose: "new findings → plan, a repeated finding → blocked" (several wordings) | — | plan 6/6 on the best wording | **regressed**: the repeated-finding guard went plan 5/5. The model can't tell "same finding" from prose | held |
| + bound by count (1st/2nd RC → plan, 3rd → blocked), prose only | — | plan 4/6 | blocked 3/6, plan-review 3/6 (miscounts) | held |
| **+ bound by count, with the count done in code** (a `PLAN-REVIEW FACTS` line, like FRONTIER FACTS) | — | **plan 4/6 and 3/6**; residual `blocked` cites the trail's own echo of the old rule ("a second Request Changes goes to the human"); 1 breakdown | **blocked 6/6** | plan 6/6 / implement 6/6 |

**What the spike shows:**
- **Facts computed in code work; prose rules are noisy in both directions.** This matches `where-judgement-happens.md:201` ("put the rule-class calls in code: escalate at the loop bound…") and the FRONTIER FACTS precedent (stage-router.js:96-104).
- **The verdict counter is cheap and needs no new parser.**
  - The contract already requires plan-review comments to start `### Plan Review Verdict` (prompt-contract.js:28).
  - `extractVerdict` exists (plan-review-round-trips.js:268).
  - Legacy trails like LIN-2950 (`## Plan-review (round 2) — Request Changes`) need a first-line fallback, because `extractVerdict` returns null on them.
  - Autopilot step records start with `**Autopilot`, so a heading test excludes them.
- **"Never route past an unanswered verdict to breakdown or implementation" must stay in the wording.** Dropping it brought back `breakdown` picks.

---

### Per-layer audit

**L1. Router prompt fragments (lib/stage-router.js:77-265)**
- Shared byte-for-byte by the writer-off full template (meta-prompt-template.js:89) and the writer-on `buildRouterPrompt` (:294).
- The bound text is at :196-199.
- A change must keep the shared-fragment property and regenerate the 8 byte snapshots in `tests/fixtures/stage-router-prompts/` (regenerator `scripts/eval/regen-stage-router-snapshots.mjs`) and `scripts/eval/meta-prompt.baseline.txt`. That is an intended diff, reviewed as text.

**L2. Router inputs (formatIssueContext, openrouter.js:649; assembleMetaPromptArgs :786)**
- There is no relation data at issue level today.
- Computed facts enter the prompt as a "deterministic, do not re-derive" block (frontierFactsBlock, stage-router.js:96). A plan-review fact block should follow that pattern, computed beside `assembleNodeFacts` (recommendation-facts.js:89).

**L3. Providers (fetchRecommendationContext)**
- **Linear** (index.js:1157 → fetchIssueContext :821): add issue-level `inverseRelations { nodes { type issue { identifier title state { name type } } } }` and normalise it to `issue.blockedBy`. The children's selection already fetches the same shape (:455-466).
- **Local** has relations (`_relationConnections`, local/index.js:527-551) but doesn't put them in fetchIssueContext (:235-290). Add them there.
- **GitHub, GitHub Projects and Jira** have no typed relations (github/index.js:53, :265; jira :512). Nothing to do, and the render is gated on presence.

**L4. formatIssueContext consumers.** openrouter.js:788 (router and meta), brief.js:57, recap.js:37, scan.js:84, task-chat-template.js:39, plus eval scripts.
- All of them gain the line only when the issue has blockers.
- Caches hash named fields only (recap-cache.js:44-70, scan-fingerprint.js:138-160), so nothing churns.

**L5. Parse and stream (stage-router.js:310-339; openrouter.js:874-955, 970-1215, 1769)**
- D2 belongs in the seam: one check that rejects a kind in `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION`, used by `parseRouteDecision` and by full-mode `parseRecommendationResponse`.
- Full mode's unknown-name → `custom` behaviour stays as it is. That is a separate behaviour, and the ticket only asks about `retro`.
- **D1 fix:** after the final parse, if the stream emitted no reasoning, emit one reasoning delta with `parsed.reasoning`. This is the same catch-up pattern the prompt section already uses (openrouter.js:1186-1192). The header grammar then has one owner (the seam), and no second regex is added.

**L6. Implementation template (prompt-template-defs.js:883-944)**
- The process is code-owned on every path (LIN-3299), so text added here reaches routed, pinned and fixed dispatches alike.
- Mirror the plan template's revision section (:269-277), and make Workflow steps 3 and 7 conditional, so the brief no longer says "Open a PR" in a fix round.

**L7. Parallel deciders: the autopilot's own copy of the bound.** autopilot-kickoff.js:517 and docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md:61-64, :80-82. These must move with L1, or the autopilot keeps parking at the second round on its own reading.

**L8. The planner's own bound (prompt-template-defs.js:277)**
- It currently reads "a plan that comes back a second time still carrying the same findings escalates to a human".
- It is the in-stage home for "same finding" judgement, and Opus reads the findings in full. Reword it to agree with the count: a third verdict escalates, and a repeated finding is answered or fixed in this pass.

**L9. Size freeze (tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js)**
- Every frozen ceiling sits exactly at its file size: stage-router.js 45728 B, prompt-template-defs.js 127237 B, prompt-templates.js 20707 B. `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES` is 575524.
- Text added must be paid by text removed in the same change. Named candidates:
  - the now-stale "behaviour deliberately unchanged / defects fixed later" paragraphs (stage-router.js:12-15, :301-303);
  - the history clause in implementation guideline 6 (prompt-template-defs.js, "This extends the acceptance-witness discipline…");
  - the bound bullets themselves, which can be rewritten shorter.
- The autopilot kickoff and manual are not frozen.

**L10. Tests and evals that pin current behaviour**
- Bound text: openrouter.test.js:986-990, :3405.
- Present-behaviour pins for D1 and D2: stage-router.test.js, per the LIN-3304 close-out. These flip from "present" to "fixed".
- `plan-review-gate.json`: request-changes-2 expects `blocked` today. It becomes `plan`, plus a new 3rd-RC case expecting `blocked`.

### Closing the set
**Searches run:**
- The bound: `SECOND Request Changes|revision cycle|second time still carrying|third pass` over lib, routes, docs, scripts and tests.
- `formatIssueContext(`.
- `fetchRecommendationContext`.
- `new StreamingSectionParser`: one site, openrouter.js:1064.
- `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION`.
- `kind:decision`.
- Every dispatched prompt for the LIN-3304, LIN-3140 and LIN-2950 trials, read through the proxy.

**Checked and left alone:**
- **docs/papers/\*\*:** historical record.
- **scripts/survey-hides-prompts.mjs:70:** a paper script whose anchor already went stale when LIN-3304 moved the text.
- **plan-review-round-trips.js:26:** a historical comment.
- **The brief writer's `copied-router` guard:** cause C is fixed without passing router text, so John's open ruling on "may a brief name what the router found" is not needed.

**The set would be wrong if:**
- another served prompt restates the plan-review bound in words my grep missed (e.g. "loop limit"). The passage runner and worker lane prompts came back empty for these terms.
- a non-Linear provider exposes relations under another field.

### Options considered
| Option | For | Against |

That was research cause 1 ("it also misleads the other way… the router can't see that LIN-2947 is Done"), and it is still open. **Inside** (class: research cause 1, relations reaching the router; and the measure's "sending an engineering call to John"). The fix is implementation's call. Either way, re-measure.

**F2. The fixtures conflate two variables, and some do not match their names.**
- All 8 LIN-2950-based bundles carry `blockedBy: []`, but real LIN-2950 has three resolved `blocks` relations. The plan (S7) said "Bundles carry `issue.blockedBy`."

So every revised/hold state is measured with the blocked-prose confound on top, and the bar cannot separate "the facts don't work" from F1. Fix: give the LIN-2950 bundles their real `blockedBy`, and build the LIN-3309 and PR-1603 states on their own trails (the PR-1603 bundle is already in `plan-review-gate.json`). **Inside** (class: the plan's pass bar, S7).

**F3. The FC decision's carry-ins are not done.**

I checked: a trail of 3 RC, then "Hold until X.", then "OK, go on." renders both replies, and rule 2 matches first. Say "the newest reply" in rules 2 and 5.
- (b) No fixture for the newest-reply case.
- (c) No fixture for count 2 plus a revision (this ticket's own state).
- (d) No fixture for a ruling posted as a comment by the FC.

**Inside** (the FC decision is part of this ticket's scope).

**F4. `revised` reads the first `Revision N` label, not the highest.** `description.match(REVISION_LABEL_RE)` takes the first match. If a description holds "Revision 2 — addresses plan-review F1." and then "Revision 3 — addresses plan-review F2." with 2 verdicts, the code returns `revisionN: 2, revised: false` (I checked), so the route is `plan`, which redoes finished work. The plan said "reads the highest N". Use the max over `matchAll` (the regex needs the `g` flag). **Inside** (S2).

**Inside** (the plan's Tests 1 and 2).

**F6. The proof is incomplete against the plan's own bar.** These are missing:
- the HEAD K=6 baseline column;
- the full-corpus regression check (the 66 existing fixtures, aggregate ≤ 2.0 points, no fixture down 3 or more);
- the run on the workspace's router model.

**Inside** (the plan's pass bar and research step 7).

**Class check.** F1 is one instance of a class: the router reads "blocked" from description prose when the relationship data disagrees. Step 2 already says to detect blocked "NOT from" prose, and the model ignores it. The other formatIssueContext consumers (brief, recap, scan) only gain the line and make no routing decision, so the only inside sibling is the router itself. I found no other sibling.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside, gate:** the pass bar on the shipping routing-only path (revised → `plan-review`, round-2/after-ruling → `plan`, no build routes). It currently fails. Discharge: re-run `ARMS=3 K=6 ROUTING_ONLY=1` after F1/F2, with numbers in the PR. A test can measure this, so it does not qualify for the post-merge lane.

- **Inside:** D1 in the live UI. Discharge: one streamed recommendation whose reply uses `**Reasoning**` shows reasoning text in the panel.
- **Inside, post-merge observation:** planners write the exact `Revision N — addresses plan-review …` line. Why no pre-merge check proves it: it is model compliance on future live plans. Monitor: the `Revision landed since the latest verdict:` line in the router prompt (trace/oplog) reading `no` on a trail where a revision comment follows the latest verdict.

### Verdict
**Request Changes.** Next action: `implementation` on this PR (#1748, continue the branch). Fix F1–F6 and re-run the pass bar. The harmful-route miss has a concrete cause in this ticket's own scope, so it does not need a ruling from John yet. If the bar is still missed after F1 and F2, then it goes to John as one question, per the plan.

1. **F1's deferral belongs in code, not prose.** When no reply follows the latest verdict, the code's route is the route; don't send that case to the model. In the eval the model sent revised states to `blocked` 6 of 6 times despite the facts. More wording won't change that.

issue.title: Improve the next-stage choice
issue.description:
Since LIN-3304, the next-stage choice has its own place. Now make it good.

In the first live trials (4 Oct; summary on LIN-3289), the work inside each stage was strong. Every slip was a judgement between stages:

* After a Request Changes review, the fix round got a fresh-start brief that didn't know about its PR or the review's findings.
* Engineering calls went to John as decisions: LIN-2950 was routed to him after plan review, and close-out filed LIN-3303. Harbour has one developer and one user. John decides product and intent; the agent decides engineering.
* The router never sees a ticket's relations (was LIN-3301).
* Two small defects turned up while isolating it: a `**Reasoning**` heading blanks the streamed recommendation (was LIN-3305), and `retro` is accepted as a route (was LIN-3306).

Measure first, from real cases (was LIN-3307), then improve against that measure. A wrong route is one that would harm the work: closing with findings still open, redoing finished work, or building without understanding. A wrong route matters; a suboptimal one is fine.

This is one coherent change. Keep it small, and finish it here rather than splitting it into follow-ups.

---

## Implementation Plan

Revision 3 — addresses plan-review findings.

One PR, fits one session.

## Research notes: LIN-3309, improve the next-stage choice (4 Oct, HEAD `98f766cc`)

**Staleness check.** Nothing has landed on `origin/main` since this ticket was created (14:08). `git log --since=2026-10-04T14:08:27Z` is empty, and HEAD is still the LIN-3304 merge, so every file:line below is at `98f766cc`.

**Sizing.** This is sized for one developer. LIN-3304's research was cut back for being about 10 times too big, so this recommends one PR with no programme around it. The measure is a handful of real cases plus unit tests.

---

### 1. The measure, from real cases

**Rule.** A route is wrong when it would harm the work: closing with findings still open, redoing finished work, building without understanding, or (from this ticket's own list) sending an engineering call to John. A suboptimal route counts as fine.

**How the cases were replayed.** Each real case was run through the live routing-only prompt (`buildRouterPrompt`, the writer-on path) on `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` at temperature 0, K=3–6 runs each. The spike script is in my scratchpad, not committed. Two cases were also replayed live through the proxy's `GET /issues/:id/recommend` on John's workspace settings.

| Case | State at the decision | Harmful routes | Right | HEAD result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **LIN-2950**, trail cut at 08:55:09 on 3 Oct, just after plan-review round 2 | 2nd Request Changes. Both findings are new (F1 drift from #1731, R4 a hole the revision opened); the reviewer says "neither needs a human preference" | `blocked` (engineering call to John); `breakdown`/`implementation` (building past open findings); `plan-review` (re-reviewing an unrevised plan) | `plan` | **blocked 5/6**, 5/5 and 3/3 across runs. Live proxy replay today: `blocked` |
| **LIN-2954**, live | Blocked by LIN-2950, 2949 and 2948, all In Progress | `research`/`plan`/`implementation` (work done now gets redone once the blockers land) | `blocked` | **research 2/3**. Live proxy replay: `research`, reasoning "Blockers: ✓ None" |
| **LIN-3304 fix round**, dispatch `dd572e67` | Review Request Changes; route was `implementation` (right) | The brief: it said "Branch… Open a PR" and nothing about the PR or the findings | brief tells the agent to continue the existing PR and answer each finding | Brief **identical to the first-pass one** apart from the Goal wording (diffed against `adb91024`). The agent recovered only because the ticket thread said "existing branch" |
| Guard `PR-1603-request-changes-1` | 1st Request Changes | anything but `plan` | `plan` | plan 6/6 |
| Guard `PR-1603-verdict-approve` | Approve | `plan-review`, `plan` | `implementation` | implementation 6/6 |
| Guard "third Request Changes" (the request-changes-2 bundle plus a 3rd verdict) | 3rd Request Changes, same finding | `plan`, `plan-review` (a loop) | `blocked` | blocked 4/6 |
| D1 (deterministic) | a `**Reasoning**` reply on the stream path | 0 live reasoning events | ≥1 | **0 events** (`StreamingSectionParser` waits for `## Reasoning\n`, openrouter.js:897); final parse still returns `plan` |
| D2 (deterministic) | `→ **retro**` | accepted | rejected | **accepted**: `routeStage` → `retro`, and `deriveDispatchKind('retro')` → `retro` |

**Does the measure track the real outcome? Yes, for these cases.** It reads red where the trials went wrong: both live replays reproduced the trial routes. It reads green on the guards. Two limits:

- **Noise.** Run-to-run noise on this model is about ±2 of 6 on the same prompt. The HEAD guard for request-changes-2 read 3/5, 3/5 and then 6/6 `blocked`. So small K proves little; use K=6 and look for shifts of 3 or more.
- **Which model.** My runs used the default router model, but John's workspace routes on its own setting. The two proxy replays did run on that setting and agree.

### 2. What causes each slip (verified)

**A. The router never sees relations (LIN-2954; also LIN-2950).**
- `ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY` selects relations only for children, grandchildren and parent.children, never for the issue itself (providers/linear/index.js:363-560).
- `formatIssueContext` renders none (openrouter.js:649-775).
- Router Step 2 tells the model to "detect this from the blocking relationship" (stage-router.js:166), so it guesses from prose.
- LIN-2950 shows the cost the other way round: its description says "Blocked until the sketches conversation is Done". LIN-2947 *is* Done, but the router can't see that, so it reasons "explicitly blocked" in most runs.

**B. The plan-review loop bound sends engineering findings to John (LIN-2950).**
- stage-router.js:199: "A SECOND Request Changes … → recommend `blocked`".
- The autopilot carries the same rule in its own prose (autopilot-kickoff.js:517; manual :61-64, :80-82), which is why it parked LIN-2950 at 08:56.
- What the record says about the bound:
  - It dates from LIN-1603 (`7f1efdb8`, 26 Jul).
  - `docs/papers/harbour/review-loops.md:21-30`: a send-back "asks for a member, not a design… None needed code to answer".
